title: NCLEX Quick Start: Safety & Infection Control(en,exam)
details:
A set of short, high-impact NCLEX-style flashcard modules.
Front = clinical prompt. Back = rule/priority + key takeaway + common trap.
No tests, no tags—pure practice for safe decision-making.

modules.moduleDescription: Fundamentals for NCLEX: standard & transmission-based precautions, safety, delegation, and priority-setting.

cards.title: Standard Precautions: what always applies?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assume blood/body fluids are potentially infectious for every patient.
Takeaway: Hand hygiene + PPE as exposure risk dictates; not based on diagnosis.

cards.title: Hand hygiene: soap vs alcohol rub
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Alcohol rub for routine decontamination; soap+water for visible soil/spores.
Trap: C. difficile/norovirus → soap+water, not just gel.

cards.title: 5 moments for hand hygiene
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Before touching patient; before aseptic task; after body fluid risk; after touching patient; after touching surroundings.
Takeaway: Room items count as “surroundings”.

cards.title: Gloving: when to change
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Change gloves between tasks and after contact with contaminated material.
Trap: Same patient ≠ same gloves if you move from dirty → clean site.

cards.title: Donning PPE order
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Gown → mask/respirator → goggles/face shield → gloves.
Takeaway: Gloves last so cuffs cover gown wrists.

cards.title: Doffing PPE order
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Gloves → goggles/face shield → gown → mask/respirator; then hand hygiene.
Trap: Remove respirator last after leaving airborne room (if required by policy).

cards.title: Clean vs sterile technique
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Clean reduces microbes; sterile eliminates all and maintains sterile field.
Takeaway: Sterile for invasive procedures (e.g., catheter insertion).

cards.title: Sterile field: what contaminates it?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: 1-inch edge is contaminated; anything below waist/out of sight is contaminated.
Trap: Reaching over field contaminates it—go around.

cards.title: Opening sterile packages
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Open away from you first, then sides, then toward you.
Takeaway: Keeps arms from crossing over sterile field.

cards.title: Surgical mask vs N95
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Surgical mask blocks droplets; N95 (fit-tested) for airborne particles.
Trap: TB/measles/varicella → N95 (or PAPR), not surgical mask.

cards.title: Airborne precautions: key steps
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Negative-pressure room + N95/PAPR; door closed.
Takeaway: Patient wears surgical mask during transport.

cards.title: Droplet precautions: key steps
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Surgical mask within ~3–6 ft (1–2 m) + private room if possible.
Trap: Droplet ≠ N95 unless aerosol-generating procedure.

cards.title: Contact precautions: key steps
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Gown+gloves on entry; dedicate equipment; clean high-touch surfaces.
Takeaway: Remove PPE before leaving room.

cards.title: C. difficile precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Contact + soap-and-water handwashing + sporicidal disinfectant.
Trap: Alcohol gel doesn’t kill spores reliably.

cards.title: MRSA/VRE precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Contact precautions; focus on hand hygiene and dedicated equipment.
Takeaway: Screen/notify per facility policy.

cards.title: TB precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Airborne isolation; N95; negative pressure.
Trap: “Latent TB” without symptoms usually doesn’t need isolation.

cards.title: Varicella (chickenpox) precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Airborne + contact; N95 and gown/gloves.
Takeaway: Immune staff preferred.

cards.title: Measles (rubeola) precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Airborne; N95; negative pressure.
Trap: Vaccine status matters—nonimmune should not enter.

cards.title: RSV precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Contact + droplet often used (especially pediatrics); follow facility policy.
Takeaway: Emphasize hand hygiene, gowns, gloves.

cards.title: Meningococcal meningitis precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Droplet for first 24 hours after effective antibiotics.
Trap: Remove droplet too early → exposure risk.

cards.title: Sharps safety: recapping needles
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Do not recap; if unavoidable, one-hand scoop technique.
Takeaway: Activate safety device immediately.

cards.title: Needlestick injury: first actions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Wash area (no squeezing), report immediately, follow post-exposure protocol.
Trap: Don’t delay reporting “until end of shift”.

cards.title: Biohazard disposal: what goes where?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sharps in puncture-proof container; blood-soaked items in biohazard bag.
Takeaway: Keep sharps container at point of use.

cards.title: Isolation signage and communication
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Post correct precaution signs; explain PPE/isolation to patient/family.
Trap: Missing signage → staff noncompliance.

cards.title: PPE with chemo/hazardous drugs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use chemo-rated gloves and gown; closed-system transfer if available.
Takeaway: Dispose per hazardous waste policy.

cards.title: Fall risk: universal prevention
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Low bed, non-skid footwear, clutter-free path, call light in reach.
Trap: Don’t leave high-risk patient unattended in bathroom.

cards.title: Post-fall: what to do first
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess for injury (neuro/vitals/pain) before moving; notify provider per policy.
Takeaway: Complete incident report; document objectively.

cards.title: Restraints: last resort rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use least restrictive measure after alternatives fail and risk is immediate.
Trap: Convenience is never an indication.

cards.title: Restraints: required checks
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Frequent circulation/skin/ROM/toileting/nutrition checks per policy.
Takeaway: Remove ASAP; document behavior and interventions.

cards.title: Restraint order timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Time-limited provider order required; renew per regulation/policy.
Trap: PRN restraint orders are not acceptable.

cards.title: Seclusion vs restraint
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Seclusion confines patient alone; restraint limits movement.
Takeaway: Both require close monitoring and documentation.

cards.title: Suicide precautions: environment
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Remove ligature risks; 1:1 observation if ordered; safe room.
Trap: “Contract for safety” is not sufficient alone.

cards.title: Fire safety: RACE
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rescue, Alarm, Contain, Extinguish/Evacuate.
Takeaway: Know unit exits and fire pulls.

cards.title: Fire extinguisher: PASS
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep.
Trap: Don’t turn your back on the fire when exiting.

cards.title: Oxygen use: fire risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: No smoking/open flames; secure cylinders; avoid petroleum-based products.
Takeaway: Post oxygen-in-use signage.

cards.title: Electrical safety: bed and equipment
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Keep equipment dry; inspect cords; use grounded outlets.
Trap: Don’t use extension cords for medical devices.

cards.title: Latex allergy: key precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use latex-free gloves/supplies; avoid latex-containing equipment.
Takeaway: Prior reactions to bananas/avocados can hint at latex sensitivity.

cards.title: Patient identification: two identifiers
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use two identifiers (e.g., name + DOB) before meds/procedures.
Trap: Room number is not an identifier.

cards.title: Medication rights: core set
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Right patient, drug, dose, route, time; plus right documentation, reason, response.
Takeaway: Check allergies every time.

cards.title: High-alert meds: double-check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Independent double-check for insulin, heparin, opioids, chemo (per policy).
Trap: “I already know the dose” → still verify.

cards.title: Look-alike/sound-alike meds
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Read label 3 times; use Tall Man lettering when available.
Takeaway: Clarify unclear orders.

cards.title: Medication reconciliation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Compare home meds with new orders at transitions of care.
Trap: Omissions are common—verify OTC/herbals too.

cards.title: Do-not-crush meds
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Do not crush extended-release/enteric-coated meds.
Takeaway: Ask pharmacy for liquid/alternate form.

cards.title: Enteral tube meds: key steps
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stop feeding if required; flush before/between/after meds.
Trap: Mix meds together → clogging/incompatibility.

cards.title: IV compatibility basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Check compatibility before Y-site mixing; use separate line if incompatible.
Takeaway: When in doubt, consult pharmacy.

cards.title: Blood transfusion: verification
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Two-person/ID verification; match patient, unit, type, expiration.
Trap: Never start transfusion without baseline vitals.

cards.title: Transfusion reaction: first action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stop transfusion, keep IV open with normal saline, notify provider/blood bank.
Takeaway: Return tubing/blood per protocol.

cards.title: Specimen collection: label timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Label at bedside immediately after collection.
Trap: Pre-labeling can cause serious errors.

cards.title: Chain of custody specimens
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Document every handoff; seal container; follow legal protocol.
Takeaway: Used for drug screens/forensics.

cards.title: HIPAA: minimum necessary
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Share only what’s needed for care/operations; verify identity.
Trap: Discussing patients in elevators = violation.

cards.title: Consent: nurse role
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Witness signature and ensure patient is informed; provider explains procedure.
Takeaway: If questions remain, stop and call provider.

cards.title: Advance directives: what to do
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Verify presence; place in chart; honor within scope/law.
Trap: Family wishes can’t override a competent patient’s directive.

cards.title: DNR vs full code
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: DNR limits resuscitation; it does not mean “no treatment”.
Takeaway: Provide comfort and indicated therapies.

cards.title: Priority setting: ABCs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Airway, Breathing, Circulation guide urgency.
Trap: A scary symptom with stable ABCs may wait behind an airway issue.

cards.title: Priority setting: Maslow
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Physiological needs before safety, love/belonging, esteem, self-actualization.
Takeaway: Safety often competes closely with physiology.

cards.title: Priority setting: acute vs chronic
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Acute/unstable beats chronic/stable.
Trap: New confusion can be acute even if vitals look okay.

cards.title: Priority setting: unexpected findings
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Unexpected/abnormal after a procedure gets priority.
Takeaway: Think complications first.

cards.title: Delegation: RN vs LPN vs UAP
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: RN assesses/teaches/evaluates; LPN performs focused care; UAP does routine tasks.
Trap: Never delegate assessment or teaching.

cards.title: Delegation: stable vs unstable
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Delegate to LPN/UAP only for stable patients with predictable outcomes.
Takeaway: Unstable or new admission stays with RN.

cards.title: Delegation: what UAP can report
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: UAP can collect data (VS, I&O) and report abnormalities; RN interprets.
Trap: UAP cannot triage or adjust oxygen.

cards.title: Incident report: documentation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Document facts in chart; complete incident report separately per policy.
Trap: Don’t write “incident report completed” in chart.

cards.title: Documentation: objective language
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Chart what you see/hear/do; use quotes for statements.
Takeaway: Avoid blame or assumptions.

cards.title: SBAR communication
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation.
Trap: Don’t skip your assessment—providers need your clinical picture.

cards.title: Critical labs: response
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Verify, notify provider promptly, document time/response, implement orders.
Takeaway: Escalate if you can’t reach provider.

cards.title: Time management: cluster care
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Group tasks to reduce room entries while maintaining safety.
Trap: Clustering never justifies skipping reassessments.

cards.title: Infection prevention: foley care
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Maintain closed system; keep bag below bladder; daily perineal care.
Takeaway: Remove catheter ASAP to prevent CAUTI.

cards.title: CAUTI prevention: indications only
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Foley only for retention, critical I&O, surgery, wounds, comfort in end-of-life.
Trap: “Convenience” or incontinence alone isn’t an indication.

cards.title: Central line infection prevention
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Scrub the hub; sterile dressing changes; CHG skin prep.
Takeaway: Watch for redness, drainage, fever.

cards.title: Pressure injury prevention: turning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Reposition at least q2h (or per plan), offload heels, manage moisture.
Trap: Red, nonblanching skin = stage 1 warning.

cards.title: Bathing: CHG use
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use CHG baths for certain lines/ICU per policy to reduce CLABSI.
Trap: Avoid CHG on mucous membranes/eyes.

cards.title: Ventilator-associated pneumonia prevention
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: HOB 30–45°, oral care, suction PRN, daily sedation vacation per protocol.
Takeaway: Aspiration prevention is key.

cards.title: Aspiration precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Upright during/after meals; check gag/swallow; thickened liquids if ordered.
Trap: Feed a lethargic patient → high aspiration risk.

cards.title: Food safety: neutropenic precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid raw/undercooked foods; wash produce; safe water sources.
Takeaway: Prevent foodborne infection.

cards.title: Vaccines: live vs inactivated
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Live vaccines avoided in severe immunosuppression; inactivated are generally safe.
Trap: Check timing after high-dose steroids.

cards.title: TB skin test vs IGRA
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: PPD needs 48–72h reading; IGRA is blood test often for BCG-vaccinated.
Takeaway: Positive screen needs CXR follow-up.

cards.title: Waste segregation: chemo vs biohazard
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Chemo waste is separate from standard biohazard.
Trap: Don’t toss chemo tubing into regular red bag.

cards.title: Radiation safety: time-distance-shielding
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Minimize time, maximize distance, use shielding.
Takeaway: Wear dosimeter if required.

cards.title: Internal radiation therapy: visitor rules
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Limit visitors/time; pregnant/children often restricted; private room.
Trap: Handle linens/fluids as radioactive per policy.

cards.title: MRI safety: ferromagnetic risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Remove metal; screen implants; keep oxygen tanks out.
Takeaway: MRI projectile risk is real.

cards.title: Safe patient handling: body mechanics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use lift devices; wide base; keep load close; avoid twisting.
Trap: “Quick boost” without help → staff injury.

cards.title: Seizure precautions: bedside setup
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pad rails, suction/O2 ready, IV access if possible.
Takeaway: Don’t restrain during seizure.

cards.title: During seizure: what not to do
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Don’t put anything in mouth; turn to side; protect head.
Trap: Forcing objects can injure teeth/airway.

cards.title: Post-seizure priorities
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Airway/vitals, neuro check, reorient, assess injury.
Takeaway: Document duration and characteristics.

cards.title: Anaphylaxis: first priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Maintain airway; administer epinephrine IM per protocol; call rapid response.
Trap: Antihistamines are adjuncts, not first-line.

cards.title: Oxygen therapy: nasal cannula limits
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Typical max 6 L/min; higher flows need different device.
Takeaway: Humidify per policy at higher flows.

cards.title: Pulse oximetry: false readings
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Poor perfusion, nail polish, motion can skew results.
Trap: Treat the patient, not just the number.

cards.title: Temperature measurement: isolation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use dedicated/disposable equipment for isolation rooms.
Takeaway: Clean reusable devices per policy.

cards.title: Environmental cleaning: high-touch sites
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Focus on bed rails, call buttons, doorknobs, bathroom surfaces.
Trap: Shared stethoscopes can spread pathogens.

cards.title: Spill cleanup: blood/body fluids
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Wear PPE; use approved disinfectant; follow facility spill protocol.
Takeaway: Larger spills may require special kit.

cards.title: Need-to-know: reporting communicable disease
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some infections are reportable to public health; follow facility policy.
Trap: Don’t promise confidentiality beyond legal limits.

cards.title: Ethics: safe assignment
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Accept assignments within competency; seek help/training when needed.
Takeaway: Document concerns through proper chain.

cards.title: Chain of command: patient safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If concern unresolved, escalate up the chain (charge nurse → supervisor → provider).
Trap: Don’t stop at the first “no” if patient is at risk.

cards.title: Disaster triage: START basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Quick assess respirations, perfusion, mental status; tag by priority.
Takeaway: Treat greatest good for greatest number.

cards.title: Mass casualty: who gets immediate?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Airway compromise but salvageable, severe bleeding, shock signs.
Trap: Pulseless/apneic in MCI often tagged expectant.

cards.title: Ergonomics: preventing back injury
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Raise bed to working height; use team lifts; avoid bending.
Takeaway: Your safety supports patient safety.

modules.title: 1. Safety & Infection Control

modules.moduleDescription: NGN-focused clinical judgment: recognize/analyze cues, prioritize hypotheses, choose actions, and evaluate outcomes for NCLEX-style scenarios.

cards.title: NGN Step 1: Recognize cues
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Identify relevant vs irrelevant data before deciding anything.
Takeaway: Circle abnormal vitals/labs + new symptoms.
Trap: Don’t anchor on the chief complaint alone.

cards.title: Recognize cues: trend beats snapshot
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Compare to baseline and look for trends.
Takeaway: A rising RR/O2 need matters more than one “okay” value.
Trap: Ignoring gradual deterioration.

cards.title: Recognize cues: subjective + objective
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pair patient report with measurable findings.
Takeaway: Pain + diaphoresis + ECG changes > pain alone.
Trap: Dismissing symptoms because one test is normal.

cards.title: Analyze cues: cluster findings
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Group related signs to form a pattern.
Takeaway: Fever + tachycardia + hypotension + AMS → think sepsis.
Trap: Treating each symptom as separate problems.

cards.title: Analyze cues: expected vs unexpected
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Unexpected findings get priority.
Takeaway: Post-op mild pain is expected; new SOB is not.
Trap: Spending time on expected discomfort.

cards.title: Prioritize hypotheses: life threats first
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rule out airway/breathing/circulation threats first.
Takeaway: Stridor, severe dyspnea, shock signs jump the line.
Trap: Fixing minor symptoms while ABCs worsen.

cards.title: Priority rule: unstable before stable
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Unstable patients are seen first regardless of diagnosis.
Takeaway: New confusion + low BP beats chronic back pain.
Trap: First-come-first-served thinking.

cards.title: Priority rule: acute before chronic
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Acute change outranks chronic conditions.
Takeaway: Sudden chest pain beats long-standing edema.
Trap: Overweighting long problem lists.

cards.title: Priority rule: unexpected vs expected
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: New/worsening or unexpected findings are urgent.
Takeaway: New bleeding, new neuro deficit, new fever → assess now.
Trap: Assuming it’s “normal recovery.”

cards.title: ABCs: Airway first
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Threatened airway is the top priority.
Takeaway: Stridor, inability to speak, swelling → call for help.
Trap: Offering PO fluids to someone who can’t protect airway.

cards.title: Breathing: oxygenation before teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Fix oxygenation/ventilation before education.
Takeaway: Apply O2/position before coaching inhaler technique.
Trap: Teaching while SpO2 is falling.

cards.title: Circulation: shock indicators
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hypotension + tachycardia + cool clammy skin suggests shock.
Takeaway: Get vitals, IV access, provider/rapid response.
Trap: Waiting for lab confirmation first.

cards.title: Maslow: physiology before psychosocial
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Physiologic needs outrank comfort/anxiety.
Takeaway: Treat hypoglycemia before addressing fear.
Trap: Letting distress distract from low glucose.

cards.title: Safety beats comfort
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Safety risks outrank comfort requests.
Takeaway: Fall risk + dizziness → assist/bed alarm before pillows.
Trap: Leaving patient alone “for a minute.”

cards.title: Infection control priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Contain transmission before moving between patients.
Takeaway: Hand hygiene/PPE and isolate as indicated.
Trap: “Quick check” without PPE.

cards.title: First action: assess (unless immediate danger)
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: When unsure, assess before intervene.
Takeaway: New complaint → focused assessment, vitals, pain scale.
Trap: Giving meds before verifying cause.

cards.title: Exception: intervene for immediate danger
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If airway/respiration/circulation is failing, act first.
Takeaway: Start CPR for pulseless patient; don’t ‘assess more’.
Trap: Spending time rechecking for a pulse repeatedly.

cards.title: Therapeutic response: open-ended first
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use open-ended questions to gather cues.
Takeaway: “Tell me more about…” beats yes/no.
Trap: Leading questions that confirm your bias.

cards.title: SBAR: Situation is the headline
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Start with the one-sentence urgent issue.
Takeaway: “New onset chest pain with ST changes.”
Trap: Burying the emergency in background details.

cards.title: SBAR: include relevant background only
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Give only background that changes decisions.
Takeaway: Allergies, code status, key comorbidities.
Trap: Reading the entire chart to the provider.

cards.title: SBAR: Assessment = what you think is happening
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: State your clinical concern clearly.
Takeaway: “Concern for sepsis/shock.”
Trap: Reporting data with no interpretation.

cards.title: SBAR: Recommendation = what you need now
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Ask for specific orders/next steps.
Takeaway: “Request lactate, cultures, fluids, antibiotics.”
Trap: Ending with “What do you want to do?”

cards.title: Rapid Response: trigger early
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Call early for acute deterioration.
Takeaway: New hypoxia, hypotension, AMS → RRT.
Trap: Waiting until arrest.

cards.title: Pain assessment: use OPQRST
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Standardize pain cues.
Takeaway: Onset, provokes, quality, radiation, severity, time.
Trap: Treating without reassessing after intervention.

cards.title: Reassessment is part of the intervention
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Always evaluate response after action.
Takeaway: Recheck vitals, pain, lung sounds after meds/O2.
Trap: Documenting “effective” without data.

cards.title: Prioritize meds: check allergies + rights
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Medication safety is clinical judgment too.
Takeaway: Verify 6 rights + allergies before admin.
Trap: Rushing because patient is “in pain.”

cards.title: Hold the med: hypotension/bradycardia
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If parameters unsafe, hold and notify provider.
Takeaway: Beta blocker with HR 48—hold per protocol.
Trap: Giving and hoping it’s fine.

cards.title: Anticoagulant red flags
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Bleeding signs need immediate evaluation.
Takeaway: Hematuria, melena, sudden headache → assess/notify.
Trap: Attributing bleeding to “normal.”

cards.title: Hypoglycemia priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Low glucose is immediate brain threat.
Takeaway: If awake: 15g fast carbs; if NPO/unconscious: IV dextrose.
Trap: Giving insulin because “diabetic.”

cards.title: Hyperglycemia danger signs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: DKA/HHS need rapid evaluation.
Takeaway: Kussmaul, fruity breath, dehydration, AMS → urgent care.
Trap: Treating as simple “high sugar.”

cards.title: Stroke: time is brain
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: New focal neuro deficits are emergency.
Takeaway: Note last known well, activate stroke protocol.
Trap: Letting patient “sleep it off.”

cards.title: Chest pain: treat as cardiac until proven otherwise
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prioritize MI workup.
Takeaway: Sit upright, O2 if needed, ECG, notify provider.
Trap: Assuming indigestion without assessment.

cards.title: PE suspicion: sudden SOB + pleuritic pain
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Think PE with acute dyspnea + tachycardia.
Takeaway: O2, assess, notify—avoid ambulation.
Trap: Sending patient to walk to bathroom alone.

cards.title: Opioid safety: RR matters
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Respiratory depression is the lethal risk.
Takeaway: Hold opioid if RR low; consider naloxone per protocol.
Trap: Chasing pain score while RR drops.

cards.title: Sedation scale awareness
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Increasing sedation precedes respiratory failure.
Takeaway: If hard to arouse, stop sedatives and assess airway.
Trap: “He’s just tired.”

cards.title: Fluid overload cues
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Crackles + JVD + weight gain suggest overload.
Takeaway: Slow fluids, elevate HOB, notify provider.
Trap: Continuing bolus because order exists.

cards.title: Dehydration cues
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tachycardia, dry mucosa, poor turgor suggest hypovolemia.
Takeaway: Monitor I&O, orthostatics; fluids per order.
Trap: Assuming low BP is ‘normal for them’ without baseline.

cards.title: Sepsis bundle thinking
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Early recognition drives outcomes.
Takeaway: Cultures + lactate + fluids + antibiotics quickly.
Trap: Waiting for fever—sepsis can be afebrile.

cards.title: Fall risk judgment
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Any new dizziness/weakness increases fall risk.
Takeaway: Assist ambulation; call light within reach.
Trap: Letting patient “prove they can walk.”

cards.title: Restraints: last resort
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use least restrictive measures first.
Takeaway: Reorient, sitter, reduce stimuli; follow policy.
Trap: Restraining for convenience.

cards.title: Suicide risk: direct questions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Ask directly about suicidal thoughts/plan.
Takeaway: Remove hazards; 1:1 observation per policy.
Trap: Avoiding the topic out of discomfort.

cards.title: Violence risk: safety first
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protect staff/patient before de-escalation.
Takeaway: Exit route, call security, calm voice.
Trap: Turning your back or blocking the doorway.

cards.title: Delegation rule: RN keeps assessment
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Initial/ongoing assessment is RN responsibility.
Takeaway: UAP can take vitals; RN interprets abnormal results.
Trap: Delegating “assess chest pain” to UAP.

cards.title: Delegation: stable tasks to UAP
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Predictable, standard tasks can go to UAP.
Takeaway: Ambulate stable patient, hygiene, I&O.
Trap: Delegating to UAP when patient is unstable.

cards.title: Delegation: PN/LVN scope
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: PN/LVN can give meds and perform focused care on stable pts (varies by state).
Takeaway: RN assigns; RN handles complex teaching/unstable pts.
Trap: Asking PN to do discharge teaching for new diagnosis.

cards.title: Teaching priority: readiness to learn
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Teaching works only when patient is stable and receptive.
Takeaway: Address pain/anxiety first; use teach-back.
Trap: Teaching during acute distress.

cards.title: Teach-back method
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Confirm understanding by having patient explain.
Takeaway: “Show me how you’ll use the inhaler.”
Trap: Asking “Do you understand?”

cards.title: Informed consent: who obtains?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Provider obtains consent; nurse verifies.
Takeaway: Ensure patient understands and is not sedated.
Trap: Explaining procedure details beyond nursing scope.

cards.title: Refusal of care
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Competent adults may refuse.
Takeaway: Assess capacity, explain risks, document, notify provider.
Trap: Threatening or coercing the patient.

cards.title: Capacity vs competency
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Capacity is clinical and decision-specific; competency is legal.
Takeaway: Assess orientation + understanding + reasoning.
Trap: Assuming confused patient lacks capacity without assessment.

cards.title: Chain of command
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Escalate when safety is at risk.
Takeaway: Charge nurse → supervisor → provider/medical director.
Trap: Staying silent when orders are unsafe.

cards.title: Prioritization: who to see first (example)
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Choose the patient with the most urgent ABC threat.
Takeaway: New stridor > fever > pain > chronic rash.
Trap: Picking the patient who complains the loudest.

cards.title: Triage: disaster START basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Respirations/perfusion/mental status guide tags.
Takeaway: Walking wounded = minor; no breathing after airway = deceased.
Trap: Spending long time on non-survivable injuries.

cards.title: Isolation decision: symptom-based
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Initiate precautions based on symptoms until ruled out.
Takeaway: Watery diarrhea → contact; cough/fever → mask.
Trap: Waiting for lab confirmation before isolating.

cards.title: PPE order: donning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Gown → mask/respirator → goggles/face shield → gloves.
Takeaway: Gloves go last.
Trap: Putting gloves on first then contaminating them.

cards.title: PPE order: doffing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Remove most contaminated first.
Takeaway: Gloves → goggles/face shield → gown → mask; hand hygiene.
Trap: Touching the front of your mask.

cards.title: Hand hygiene: when soap & water
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use soap/water for C. diff or visibly soiled hands.
Takeaway: Alcohol gel isn’t enough for spores.
Trap: Using sanitizer only after C. diff care.

cards.title: Critical thinking: verify abnormal results
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Recheck/confirm critical values promptly.
Takeaway: Repeat BP manually; check lead placement for weird ECG.
Trap: Assuming monitor is always right.

cards.title: Documentation: chart what you saw/did
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Document facts, not opinions.
Takeaway: “Patient yelled” not “patient is rude.”
Trap: Charting blame or speculation.

cards.title: Error disclosure: report immediately
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Patient safety requires prompt reporting.
Takeaway: Notify charge/provider per policy; complete incident report.
Trap: Hiding the mistake.

cards.title: Incident report: not in chart
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Incident report is administrative, separate from medical record.
Takeaway: Chart patient condition and actions taken.
Trap: Writing “incident report completed” in chart.

cards.title: Ethics: beneficence vs autonomy
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Doing good doesn’t override patient choice.
Takeaway: Provide info; respect refusal if capacity intact.
Trap: Forcing care “for their own good.”

cards.title: Ethics: justice
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Provide fair care regardless of background.
Takeaway: Same triage standards for all.
Trap: Letting bias change priority.

cards.title: Cultural humility
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Ask, don’t assume.
Takeaway: “What does this mean for you?”
Trap: Stereotyping based on culture.

cards.title: Interpreter use
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use trained medical interpreter for limited English proficiency.
Takeaway: Avoid using children/family for consent discussions.
Trap: Relying on gestures for critical teaching.

cards.title: Vitals: which matters most?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Trends + context determine significance.
Takeaway: HR 120 after ambulation differs from HR 120 at rest.
Trap: Treating numbers without context.

cards.title: Neuro check: acute change alert
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: New confusion is a red flag.
Takeaway: Check glucose, O2, meds, infection, stroke signs.
Trap: Assuming “sundowning” without assessment.

cards.title: Airway positioning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Positioning is a first-line intervention.
Takeaway: High Fowler’s for dyspnea; recovery position for vomiting risk.
Trap: Leaving patient flat when they can’t breathe.

cards.title: Aspiration precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protect airway when swallow impaired.
Takeaway: HOB 90°, thickened liquids, suction ready.
Trap: Giving thin liquids to coughing patient.

cards.title: Post-op assessment priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ABCs + bleeding check first post-op.
Takeaway: Airway patency, SpO2, BP/HR, surgical site.
Trap: Focusing on pain score before vitals.

cards.title: Hemorrhage cues
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tachycardia may precede hypotension.
Takeaway: Look for pale, cool skin, falling urine output.
Trap: Waiting for BP to drop.

cards.title: Urine output as perfusion marker
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: UOP reflects kidney perfusion.
Takeaway: <30 mL/hr in adult is concerning.
Trap: Ignoring low UOP because patient is asleep.

cards.title: Acid-base quick read
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Ventilation problems change CO2; metabolic changes HCO3.
Takeaway: Low pH + high CO2 = respiratory acidosis.
Trap: Treating the lab without assessing breathing.

cards.title: Electrolytes: hyperkalemia danger
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: High K+ can cause lethal dysrhythmias.
Takeaway: Weakness + peaked T waves → urgent notify.
Trap: Waiting for repeat lab before ECG.

cards.title: Electrolytes: hypokalemia danger
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Low K+ increases dysrhythmia risk.
Takeaway: Muscle cramps + U waves → replace per order.
Trap: Giving loop diuretics without monitoring.

cards.title: Calcium: tetany signs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Low Ca can cause neuromuscular irritability.
Takeaway: Trousseau/Chvostek → notify.
Trap: Mistaking tingling for anxiety.

cards.title: Magnesium: toxicity
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: High Mg depresses CNS/respiration.
Takeaway: Loss of DTRs + low RR → stop Mg, prepare calcium gluconate.
Trap: Focusing only on BP.

cards.title: OB emergency: postpartum hemorrhage
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Boggy uterus = atony.
Takeaway: Fundal massage, assess lochia, notify.
Trap: Assuming heavy bleeding is normal.

cards.title: Peds dehydration: best indicator
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Weight is the best indicator of fluid status in children.
Takeaway: Compare daily weights and I&O.
Trap: Relying only on tears or mucous membranes.

cards.title: Mental health: hallucinations priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess for command hallucinations.
Takeaway: “Are the voices telling you to hurt yourself/others?”
Trap: Debating the content of hallucinations.

cards.title: Crisis communication
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use short, calm, concrete statements.
Takeaway: Reduce stimuli; offer choices.
Trap: Long explanations during agitation.

cards.title: Ethical dilemma: report impaired colleague
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Patient safety overrides loyalty.
Takeaway: Follow policy/chain; document objectively.
Trap: Covering for them to “help.”

cards.title: Quality improvement: root cause thinking
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Look for system causes, not just blame.
Takeaway: Ask “why” repeatedly to find process gaps.
Trap: Assuming one person is the whole problem.

cards.title: Clinical judgment: avoid confirmation bias
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Seek data that could disprove your first idea.
Takeaway: If you think anxiety, still check SpO2/glucose.
Trap: Only noticing data that fits your guess.

cards.title: Heuristic: worst-first mindset
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Consider the worst plausible diagnosis first.
Takeaway: Sudden headache → rule out bleed.
Trap: Labeling as migraine without neuro check.

cards.title: When to call provider: change from baseline
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Report any significant change from baseline.
Takeaway: New O2 need, new fever, new arrhythmia.
Trap: Waiting until next rounds.

cards.title: Clinical judgment: document escalation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Record who you notified and when.
Takeaway: Time-stamped SBAR and response.
Trap: Vague notes like “MD aware.”

cards.title: Prioritize labs: critical values first
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Act on critical results immediately.
Takeaway: Hypoglycemia, K+ extremes, high INR bleeding.
Trap: Filing results for later.

cards.title: NGN: link interventions to cues
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Each action should target a specific cue/problem.
Takeaway: Crackles → elevate HOB + diuretic order check.
Trap: Random interventions “to do something.”

cards.title: NGN: evaluate outcomes
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Outcomes must be measurable.
Takeaway: SpO2 ↑ to goal, pain ↓, BP stabilizes.
Trap: “Patient looks better” without numbers.

cards.title: Teamwork: closed-loop communication
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Repeat back critical info to confirm.
Takeaway: “Give 1 mg epi IV now—confirmed.”
Trap: Assuming someone heard you.

cards.title: Handoff: include safety risks
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Transfers must highlight risks.
Takeaway: Isolation, fall risk, tubes/lines, allergies.
Trap: Forgetting anticoagulants or drains.

cards.title: Medication reconciliation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Verify home meds at transitions of care.
Takeaway: Compare lists; clarify duplications.
Trap: Assuming the EHR list is accurate.

cards.title: Discharge safety: red flags
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Teach when to seek urgent care.
Takeaway: SOB, chest pain, uncontrolled bleeding, fever, neuro changes.
Trap: Giving only routine instructions.

cards.title: End-of-life: comfort focus
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Align care with goals.
Takeaway: Treat pain/dyspnea; avoid burdensome interventions.
Trap: Pushing aggressive care against wishes.

cards.title: Ethics: DNR does not mean do not treat
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: DNR limits CPR, not comfort/other treatments.
Takeaway: Continue meds/oxygen as appropriate.
Trap: Withholding all care because DNR.

cards.title: Priority question strategy
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: In priority items, choose the option that prevents harm first.
Takeaway: Safety/ABCs beat teaching/comfort.
Trap: Picking the most “complete” answer not the safest.

cards.title: Select-all-that-apply mindset
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pick all true/necessary actions; not just one best.
Takeaway: Think safety steps + monitoring + notify.
Trap: Choosing mutually exclusive options that can coexist.

cards.title: Time management: cluster care
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Combine tasks to reduce trips and errors.
Takeaway: Med pass + assessment + teaching together.
Trap: Running back and forth and missing changes.

cards.title: Acuity vs workload
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: High acuity patients need more RN time.
Takeaway: Advocate assignments based on instability.
Trap: Accepting unsafe ratios silently.

cards.title: Fatigue safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Fatigue increases error risk.
Takeaway: Use checklists, double-check high-alert meds.
Trap: Skipping verification “because I’m experienced.”

cards.title: High-alert meds: independent double-check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Insulin, heparin, opioids often require double-check.
Takeaway: Use policy; verify dose and pump settings.
Trap: Copying another nurse’s settings without verifying.

cards.title: IV pump: line tracing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Trace tubing from bag to patient.
Takeaway: Prevent wrong-line infusions.
Trap: Assuming the correct line is connected.

cards.title: Air embolism prevention
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Clamp/prime lines; occlusive dressing for central lines.
Takeaway: Left side Trendelenburg if suspected; call for help.
Trap: Sitting patient upright during line change.

cards.title: Pressure injury prevention judgment
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Risk rises with immobility, moisture, poor nutrition.
Takeaway: Turn schedule, skin checks, offload heels.
Trap: Waiting until redness becomes an ulcer.

cards.title: Restraints: circulation checks
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Restraints require frequent assessment.
Takeaway: Check skin, pulses, ROM; document per policy.
Trap: Applying and forgetting.

cards.title: Medication timing: time-critical
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some meds are time-critical (e.g., antibiotics, Parkinson’s meds).
Takeaway: Give within window; coordinate with meals.
Trap: Delaying “until I have time.”

cards.title: Anaphylaxis cues
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rapid onset airway swelling + hypotension = anaphylaxis.
Takeaway: Epi per protocol, airway support, call RRT.
Trap: Giving only antihistamine first.

cards.title: Seizure precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protect from injury, maintain airway.
Takeaway: Side-lying, time seizure, do not restrain.
Trap: Putting something in mouth.

cards.title: Post-seizure priorities
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Airway and safety after seizure.
Takeaway: Check glucose/O2, neuro status.
Trap: Forcing patient to answer questions immediately.

cards.title: Overdose: opioid vs benzo clues
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pinpoint pupils + low RR suggests opioid.
Takeaway: Naloxone for opioid; support airway for any overdose.
Trap: Focusing on pupil size and ignoring breathing.

cards.title: Patient identification
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Two identifiers before meds/procedures.
Takeaway: Name + DOB/ID band.
Trap: Using room number as identifier.

cards.title: Wrong-site prevention
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Time-out before procedures.
Takeaway: Verify patient/procedure/site.
Trap: Skipping because “we always do this.”

cards.title: Clinical judgment: ask for help early
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Early collaboration prevents crises.
Takeaway: Consult charge nurse/resources with uncertainty.
Trap: Trying to handle deterioration alone.

modules.title: 2. Clinical Judgment (NGN Core)

modules.moduleDescription: High-yield pharmacology for NCLEX: core med classes, side effects, antidotes, and patient teaching (RN/PN safe practice).

cards.title: Insulin onset: know your 'peak' risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rapid/short-acting insulin can cause hypoglycemia at peak action.
Takeaway: Time meals/snacks to peak; monitor glucose when symptoms appear. Trap: Assuming bedtime NPH has no overnight hypoglycemia risk.

cards.title: Hypoglycemia rule of 15
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If conscious and able to swallow: 15 g fast carbs, recheck in 15 minutes.
Takeaway: Repeat until >70 mg/dL, then longer-acting carb/protein. Trap: Giving juice to an unconscious patient (aspiration).

cards.title: DKA vs HHS quick meds
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: DKA/HHS treatment includes fluids then insulin; K+ drives safety.
Takeaway: Hold insulin if K+ is low; replace potassium first. Trap: Starting insulin before fluids or ignoring potassium.

cards.title: Metformin: hold for contrast
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Metformin can increase lactic acidosis risk with renal insult.
Takeaway: Hold around iodinated contrast or acute kidney injury per policy. Trap: Continuing metformin with rising creatinine/dehydration.

cards.title: Sulfonylureas: long hypoglycemia
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: These increase insulin release and can cause prolonged lows.
Takeaway: Teach consistent meals; monitor especially in older adults. Trap: Treating once and sending home without observation.

cards.title: Warfarin: INR target idea
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Warfarin effect is monitored by INR, with delayed onset.
Takeaway: Expect 2–3 day lag; bridge with heparin if ordered. Trap: Stopping heparin as soon as warfarin is started.

cards.title: Warfarin antidote
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Serious bleeding on warfarin requires reversal.
Takeaway: Vitamin K ± PCC/FFP per orders; monitor INR. Trap: Giving vitamin K for mildly elevated INR without bleeding.

cards.title: Heparin drip: aPTT/anti-Xa
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Unfractionated heparin is titrated using aPTT or anti-Xa.
Takeaway: Check labs per protocol and assess for bleeding. Trap: Using IM injections while on heparin.

cards.title: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: HIT is immune platelet drop with paradoxical thrombosis.
Takeaway: Stop all heparin, notify provider, use non-heparin anticoagulant. Trap: Assuming low platelets means ‘give platelets’ routinely.

cards.title: Enoxaparin teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: LMWH is given subcut; do not expel air bubble prefilled.
Takeaway: Inject in abdomen, rotate sites, no rubbing. Trap: Aspirating or massaging the site (bruising).

cards.title: Aspirin: bleeding + Reye
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Aspirin irreversibly inhibits platelets; avoid in children with viral illness.
Takeaway: Teach bleeding precautions and tinnitus as toxicity sign. Trap: Giving aspirin to a child with flu symptoms.

cards.title: Clopidogrel basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Antiplatelet therapy reduces thrombotic events after stent.
Takeaway: Emphasize adherence; check for bleeding/bruising. Trap: Stopping early after stent (stent thrombosis).

cards.title: Thrombolytics red flags
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Alteplase increases bleeding risk; absolute contraindications matter.
Takeaway: Assess recent surgery/bleed/stroke; monitor neuro status. Trap: Starting without checking last-known-well time in stroke.

cards.title: Nitroglycerin + PDE5 inhibitors
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Nitrates + sildenafil/tadalafil can cause life-threatening hypotension.
Takeaway: Ask about ED meds in last 24–48h; monitor BP. Trap: Giving nitro to a patient who took sildenafil today.

cards.title: Beta blockers: pulse rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Beta blockers lower HR and BP.
Takeaway: Hold/notify if HR is low per parameters; assess for bronchospasm. Trap: Giving dose despite HR 48 because ‘BP is fine’.

cards.title: Calcium channel blockers: edema
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: DHP CCBs cause peripheral edema and hypotension.
Takeaway: Monitor BP; teach swelling is common. Trap: Confusing edema with heart failure without assessing lungs.

cards.title: ACE inhibitors: cough + K+
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ACEIs can cause dry cough and hyperkalemia; risk angioedema.
Takeaway: Monitor K+/creatinine; stop and treat angioedema immediately. Trap: Giving ACEI after prior angioedema history.

cards.title: ARBs: pregnancy
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ARBs/ACEIs are teratogenic.
Takeaway: Avoid in pregnancy; verify contraception/plan. Trap: Continuing lisinopril in pregnant patient.

cards.title: Diuretics: loop vs thiazide
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Loop diuretics waste K+ and can cause ototoxicity at high doses.
Takeaway: Monitor K+, I&O, daily weight; give IV push slowly per policy. Trap: Giving furosemide rapidly IV push (ototoxicity/hypotension).

cards.title: Spironolactone: K+ sparing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Aldosterone antagonist retains potassium.
Takeaway: Avoid K+ supplements/salt substitutes; monitor K+. Trap: Treating hypokalemia with spironolactone.

cards.title: Digoxin toxicity key signs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Digoxin toxicity: nausea, vision changes, bradyarrhythmias.
Takeaway: Check apical pulse; monitor levels and K+; Digibind for severe. Trap: Giving digoxin when apical pulse is 52.

cards.title: Statins: liver + muscle
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Statins can raise LFTs and cause myopathy.
Takeaway: Report muscle pain/dark urine; avoid grapefruit with some statins. Trap: Taking with large grapefruit juice daily.

cards.title: Amiodarone: lungs + thyroid
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Amiodarone has pulmonary and thyroid toxicity.
Takeaway: Monitor PFTs, thyroid, ECG; teach photosensitivity. Trap: Ignoring new cough/SOB in amiodarone patient.

cards.title: Opioids: respiratory safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Opioids depress respiration; monitor sedation scale.
Takeaway: Hold and stimulate/notify if RR low; naloxone for overdose. Trap: Chasing pain score while RR is 8.

cards.title: Naloxone: shorter half-life
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Naloxone may wear off before opioid.
Takeaway: Re-dose/monitor for re-sedation; watch withdrawal. Trap: Discharging right after naloxone response.

cards.title: Benzodiazepines: falls
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Benzos cause sedation and confusion.
Takeaway: Use fall precautions; avoid with alcohol/opioids when possible. Trap: Giving lorazepam then letting patient ambulate alone.

cards.title: Flumazenil caution
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Flumazenil reverses benzos but can trigger seizures in chronic users.
Takeaway: Use only when indicated; monitor closely. Trap: Giving flumazenil to long-term benzo user.

cards.title: Antibiotic timing: cultures first
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Before first antibiotic dose for suspected sepsis, obtain cultures if possible.
Takeaway: Do not delay antibiotics; draw cultures quickly then start. Trap: Waiting hours for ‘perfect’ cultures while unstable.

cards.title: Vancomycin: infusion reaction
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rapid infusion can cause ‘red man syndrome’.
Takeaway: Infuse slowly per policy; monitor troughs, kidneys. Trap: Pushing vanco fast to ‘catch up’.

cards.title: Aminoglycosides: ears/kidneys
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Gentamicin is nephrotoxic and ototoxic.
Takeaway: Monitor creatinine, troughs; report tinnitus. Trap: Combining with loop diuretics without monitoring.

cards.title: Penicillin allergy: true vs intolerance
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: True anaphylaxis risk matters for cross-reactivity decisions.
Takeaway: Clarify reaction type; have emergency meds ready. Trap: Documenting ‘allergy’ as nausea and avoiding all beta-lactams forever.

cards.title: C. diff risk with antibiotics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Broad antibiotics raise C. diff risk.
Takeaway: Use contact precautions; teach handwashing with soap/water. Trap: Using alcohol gel as sole hand hygiene for C. diff.

cards.title: Steroids: hyperglycemia
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Systemic steroids raise glucose and infection risk.
Takeaway: Monitor glucose; taper if long-term; take with food. Trap: Stopping abruptly after prolonged therapy (adrenal crisis).

cards.title: Inhaled steroids: rinse mouth
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ICS can cause oral thrush.
Takeaway: Rinse mouth after use; use spacer. Trap: Treating thrush without teaching rinse.

cards.title: Albuterol: tremor + tachy
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Beta-agonists can cause tachycardia/tremor.
Takeaway: Monitor HR; avoid overuse; evaluate if no relief. Trap: Using rescue inhaler repeatedly instead of seeking help.

cards.title: Theophylline: narrow window
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Theophylline toxicity causes arrhythmias and seizures.
Takeaway: Monitor levels; avoid caffeine; watch for nausea. Trap: Assuming ‘it’s just stomach flu’ with high level.

cards.title: Antiepileptics: no abrupt stop
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stopping AEDs abruptly can trigger seizures.
Takeaway: Maintain schedule; teach adherence; check levels for some meds. Trap: Holding phenytoin because patient feels better.

cards.title: Phenytoin IV: no dextrose
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Phenytoin precipitates with dextrose; give in NS and slow.
Takeaway: Use filter; monitor BP/ECG; watch for purple glove. Trap: Running phenytoin in D5W.

cards.title: Phenytoin gums teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Phenytoin can cause gingival hyperplasia.
Takeaway: Good oral hygiene and dental care. Trap: Ignoring gum swelling as ‘normal’.

cards.title: Lithium: salt/water
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Lithium levels rise with dehydration/low sodium.
Takeaway: Maintain fluids/salt; monitor levels; toxicity tremor/confusion. Trap: Giving diuretic without monitoring lithium.

cards.title: SSRIs: serotonin syndrome
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SSRIs + other serotonergic meds can cause serotonin syndrome.
Takeaway: Watch agitation, hyperreflexia, fever; stop offending agents. Trap: Combining SSRI with MAOI without washout.

cards.title: MAOIs: tyramine crisis
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: MAOIs + tyramine cause hypertensive crisis.
Takeaway: Avoid aged cheeses/cured meats; monitor BP. Trap: Eating pepperoni pizza while on MAOI.

cards.title: Antipsychotics: NMS
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome: rigidity, fever, autonomic instability.
Takeaway: Stop drug; cool/support; notify provider urgently. Trap: Mistaking NMS for ‘flu’ after new antipsychotic.

cards.title: Clozapine: agranulocytosis
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Clozapine can cause severe neutropenia.
Takeaway: Regular CBC/ANC monitoring; report fever/sore throat. Trap: Continuing clozapine with low ANC.

cards.title: Aspirin + anticoagulant stacking
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Multiple antithrombotics raise bleeding risk.
Takeaway: Verify indication; monitor stool/urine bleeding signs. Trap: Giving PRN NSAIDs to a patient on warfarin.

cards.title: NSAIDs: kidneys + GI
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: NSAIDs can cause GI bleed and kidney injury.
Takeaway: Take with food; avoid in CKD/ulcer history. Trap: Giving ibuprofen to patient with GI bleed.

cards.title: Acetaminophen max dose
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Excess acetaminophen causes liver failure.
Takeaway: Track total daily dose from combo products. Trap: Giving extra Tylenol with Percocet without counting.

cards.title: Insulin mixing: clear to cloudy
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: When mixing regular + NPH, draw up clear then cloudy.
Takeaway: Prevents contaminating regular vial. Trap: Drawing NPH first.

cards.title: Heparin injections: no aspiration
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: For subcutaneous heparin/LMWH, do not aspirate or massage.
Takeaway: Reduces hematoma/bruising. Trap: Rubbing site to ‘distribute’ medication.

cards.title: Epinephrine for anaphylaxis route
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: First-line for anaphylaxis is IM epinephrine in thigh.
Takeaway: Do not delay for antihistamines; repeat per protocol. Trap: Giving diphenhydramine first while airway swelling progresses.

cards.title: Oxygen + opioids trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: O2 can mask hypoventilation on pulse ox.
Takeaway: Assess RR/CO2, sedation; not just SpO2. Trap: Turning up oxygen instead of treating respiratory depression.

cards.title: Insulin storage
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Unopened insulin refrigerated; opened per product guidance, room temp OK for limited days.
Takeaway: Label open date; protect from heat/freeze. Trap: Using expired opened pen ‘because it looks fine’.

cards.title: Anticoagulant bleeding assessment
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Monitor gums, urine, stool, bruising, BP/HR trends.
Takeaway: Teach soft toothbrush/electric razor. Trap: Missing occult bleed signs like black stools.

cards.title: Warfarin diet consistency
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Vitamin K intake should be consistent, not eliminated.
Takeaway: Teach stable leafy greens pattern. Trap: Sudden spinach binge causing INR drop.

cards.title: Digoxin + hypokalemia
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Low K+ increases digoxin toxicity risk.
Takeaway: Correct K+; monitor ECG and symptoms. Trap: Giving digoxin with K+ 2.9.

cards.title: Beta-agonists + hypokalemia
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Albuterol can lower serum potassium transiently.
Takeaway: Monitor K+ in high-dose neb therapy. Trap: Ignoring ectopy during continuous nebs.

cards.title: QT prolongation meds
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics, macrolides prolong QT.
Takeaway: Monitor ECG; correct Mg/K. Trap: Adding multiple QT drugs without monitoring.

cards.title: Magnesium sulfate: OB antidote
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: MgSO4 toxicity causes loss of reflexes/resp depression.
Takeaway: Monitor DTRs, RR, urine output; calcium gluconate antidote. Trap: Continuing infusion with absent patellar reflex.

cards.title: Heparin reversal
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protamine reverses heparin.
Takeaway: Use per protocol for bleeding; monitor aPTT. Trap: Giving vitamin K for heparin bleed.

cards.title: Loop diuretics: hearing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: High-dose rapid IV loop can cause ototoxicity.
Takeaway: Infuse slowly; monitor hearing complaints. Trap: Ignoring ringing ears after IV furosemide.

cards.title: ACEI first-dose hypotension
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ACEIs can cause first-dose hypotension, esp. volume depleted.
Takeaway: Assess volume; monitor BP after first dose. Trap: Giving after aggressive diuresis without BP checks.

cards.title: Beta blockers in asthma/COPD
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Nonselective beta blockers can worsen bronchospasm.
Takeaway: Prefer cardioselective; monitor wheeze/SOB. Trap: Giving propranolol to asthmatic with active wheeze.

cards.title: Insulin sliding scale trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Correction insulin is not a substitute for basal needs.
Takeaway: Ensure basal + nutrition plan; avoid ‘chasing’ glucose. Trap: Holding basal insulin because patient is NPO without orders.

cards.title: NPH peak time
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Intermediate insulin peaks later (often 4–12h).
Takeaway: Plan snacks; monitor overnight if evening dose. Trap: Skipping bedtime snack after evening NPH.

cards.title: Opioid + benzo combo risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Combined CNS depressants greatly increase overdose risk.
Takeaway: Use lowest dose; monitor closely; avoid mixing at home. Trap: Giving both PRN without reassessing sedation.

cards.title: Antibiotics: finish course
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stopping early can cause relapse/resistance.
Takeaway: Teach complete prescribed course unless directed. Trap: Saving leftover antibiotics for next time.

cards.title: Oral contraceptives + antibiotics myth nuance
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Most antibiotics don’t reduce OCP efficacy; rifampin does.
Takeaway: Teach backup contraception if on rifampin-like drugs. Trap: Telling patient all antibiotics ‘cancel birth control’.

cards.title: Rifampin: orange fluids
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rifampin colors urine/tears orange and can stain contacts.
Takeaway: Teach expected effect; monitor liver enzymes. Trap: Patient stops med thinking it’s bleeding.

cards.title: Isoniazid: B6
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: INH can cause neuropathy; give pyridoxine.
Takeaway: Teach report numbness/tingling. Trap: Ignoring neuropathy complaints.

cards.title: Heparin drip: double-check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: High-alert meds require independent double-check per policy.
Takeaway: Verify weight-based dosing and pump settings. Trap: Programming from memory without second check.

cards.title: Insulin high-alert
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Insulin is high-alert; use standardized concentrations.
Takeaway: No trailing zeros, use units clearly. Trap: Writing ‘10U’ that looks like ‘100’.

cards.title: Morphine: histamine itch
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Morphine can cause itching via histamine release.
Takeaway: Assess for allergy vs expected side effect. Trap: Charting ‘morphine allergy’ for itching only.

cards.title: Antiemetics QT
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Ondansetron can prolong QT.
Takeaway: Use caution with QT risk; monitor if high dose. Trap: Giving IV push rapidly to ‘work faster’.

cards.title: Chemotherapy extravasation alert
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some chemo is vesicant; extravasation is an emergency.
Takeaway: Stop infusion, leave catheter, follow antidote protocol. Trap: Flushing the line after patient reports burning.

cards.title: Insulin pen sharing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Insulin pens are single-patient use.
Takeaway: Never share even with new needle. Trap: Using same pen on different patients.

cards.title: Heparin line flush confusion
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Heparin flushes are different from heparin drip concentrations.
Takeaway: Label and store separately. Trap: Using heparin flush as if it were IV bolus.

cards.title: PPI vs H2 blockers
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Both reduce acid; PPIs often for ulcers/GERD; monitor for long-term risks.
Takeaway: Teach timing (before meals) for PPIs. Trap: Taking PPI only when symptoms occur.

cards.title: Glucocorticoids and infection masking
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Steroids can mask fever/inflammation.
Takeaway: Assess other infection signs; monitor WBC trend. Trap: Assuming ‘no fever’ means no infection.

cards.title: Insulin: IV vs SQ contexts
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: IV insulin acts immediately and needs close monitoring.
Takeaway: Check glucose hourly per protocol; prevent hypoglycemia. Trap: Leaving IV insulin running during transport without checks.

cards.title: Anticoagulants + neuraxial anesthesia
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Spinal/epidural with anticoagulants risks spinal hematoma.
Takeaway: Follow timing guidelines; report back pain/weakness. Trap: Restarting LMWH too soon after epidural removal.

cards.title: Beta blockers: do not stop abruptly
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Abrupt stop can cause rebound tachy/angina.
Takeaway: Taper per provider; reinforce adherence. Trap: Patient stops because HR is ‘too low’ without consult.

cards.title: Levothyroxine: empty stomach
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Absorption best on empty stomach, same time daily.
Takeaway: Separate from calcium/iron. Trap: Taking with breakfast and supplements together.

cards.title: Thyroid meds: symptom matching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Overreplacement causes hyper symptoms; under causes hypo symptoms.
Takeaway: Teach monitor palpitations, weight changes. Trap: Assuming fatigue means dose is too high.

cards.title: Heparin + platelets monitoring schedule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Monitor platelets for HIT risk in first 5–10 days.
Takeaway: Report sudden drop or thrombosis signs. Trap: Ignoring new DVT while platelets fall.

cards.title: Warfarin pregnancy contraindication
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Warfarin crosses placenta and is teratogenic.
Takeaway: Use heparin/LMWH in pregnancy when anticoag needed. Trap: Continuing warfarin during pregnancy.

cards.title: Insulin sick-day rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: During illness, continue basal insulin; monitor more often.
Takeaway: Check ketones if high glucose; hydrate. Trap: Stopping insulin because ‘not eating’.

cards.title: Antibiotic allergy cross-reactivity trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cephalosporin cross-reactivity is low but caution with true anaphylaxis.
Takeaway: Assess severity; use alternatives when needed. Trap: Automatically giving cephalosporin after anaphylaxis history.

cards.title: Opioid constipation prevention
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Opioids slow gut; constipation is expected.
Takeaway: Start stool softener/laxative regimen early. Trap: Waiting for day 5 without BM to treat.

cards.title: Anticoagulants: IM injections
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: IM injections increase hematoma risk when anticoagulated.
Takeaway: Use SQ/IV routes when possible; apply pressure longer. Trap: Giving IM vaccine without precautions.

cards.title: Insulin correction timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Give rapid-acting insulin with meals unless NPO and ordered.
Takeaway: Match dose to carbs and glucose. Trap: Giving correction then tray arrives 1 hour later.

cards.title: Insulin pump basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pump delivers rapid insulin only; interruption causes quick hyperglycemia.
Takeaway: Assess site/pump function if high glucose. Trap: Assuming pump patient can skip basal.

cards.title: Epi pen teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: IM thigh through clothing is OK; hold in place per device instructions.
Takeaway: Call EMS after use; watch rebound. Trap: Not calling 911 because symptoms improved.

cards.title: Nitro storage
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Nitro tablets lose potency with air/light.
Takeaway: Keep in original dark bottle; replace per expiry. Trap: Carrying loose tablets in pillbox for months.

cards.title: Diuretic timing: morning dose
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Diuretics cause frequent urination.
Takeaway: Give earlier in day; protect sleep and falls. Trap: Giving furosemide at bedtime.

cards.title: ACEI/ARB: renal artery stenosis
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Can worsen renal function in bilateral renal artery stenosis.
Takeaway: Monitor creatinine rise after start. Trap: Ignoring sharp creatinine bump.

cards.title: Antibiotics: anaphylaxis timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Anaphylaxis can occur quickly after dose.
Takeaway: Monitor closely with first doses; have epinephrine ready. Trap: Leaving patient alone right after IV antibiotic start.

cards.title: Vancomycin: nephrotoxic combos
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Risk increases with other nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, contrast).
Takeaway: Trend creatinine and levels. Trap: Continuing vanco despite rising creatinine without notifying.

cards.title: Gentamicin peak/trough idea
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Aminoglycoside dosing relies on peaks/troughs to limit toxicity.
Takeaway: Draw at correct times; monitor hearing. Trap: Drawing ‘random’ levels and adjusting wrongly.

cards.title: Steroid taper rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: After long-term steroids, taper to prevent adrenal insufficiency.
Takeaway: Teach weakness, hypotension risk if stopped abruptly. Trap: Patient stops prednisone suddenly after weeks.

cards.title: Albuterol vs levalbuterol
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Both bronchodilate; overuse indicates poor control.
Takeaway: Teach rescue vs controller meds. Trap: Using albuterol daily instead of inhaled steroid controller.

cards.title: Insulin: no U-100 vs U-500 mixup
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Different concentrations require different syringes/dosing.
Takeaway: Double-check product; use correct device. Trap: Measuring U-500 with U-100 syringe.

cards.title: Warfarin: many interactions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Many meds/herbals affect INR (antibiotics, amiodarone, NSAIDs).
Takeaway: Teach to check before new meds; monitor INR more often. Trap: Starting ‘herbal cleanse’ without telling clinic.

cards.title: Heparin: signs of internal bleed
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Back pain, abdominal pain, hypotension can signal bleed.
Takeaway: Assess vitals, labs; notify urgently. Trap: Focusing only on skin bruises.

cards.title: Digoxin: apical 1 full minute
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess apical pulse for 60 seconds before giving.
Takeaway: Hold per parameters; monitor rhythm. Trap: Counting 15 seconds and multiplying.

cards.title: Statins: pregnancy
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Statins generally avoided in pregnancy.
Takeaway: Verify pregnancy status in childbearing age. Trap: Continuing statin with confirmed pregnancy.

cards.title: NSAIDs: asthma sensitivity
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some asthmatics are NSAID-sensitive (bronchospasm).
Takeaway: Assess history; monitor breathing after dose. Trap: Giving ketorolac to aspirin-sensitive asthma.

cards.title: Acetaminophen antidote timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: N-acetylcysteine is antidote for overdose; earlier is better.
Takeaway: Get acetaminophen level; treat per protocol. Trap: Waiting for symptoms before acting.

cards.title: Ondansetron constipation/headache
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Common side effects; monitor bowel patterns.
Takeaway: Encourage fluids/fiber if appropriate. Trap: Ignoring severe constipation in post-op patient.

cards.title: Antipsychotics: EPS vs TD
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: EPS can be acute; TD is late and may be irreversible.
Takeaway: Monitor abnormal movements; treat EPS early. Trap: Assuming lip smacking will go away on its own.

cards.title: Benztropine for EPS
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Anticholinergic can treat acute dystonia/parkinsonism from antipsychotics.
Takeaway: Watch anticholinergic side effects. Trap: Giving to patient with glaucoma/urinary retention without caution.

cards.title: Lithium level timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Draw trough level ~12 hours after last dose.
Takeaway: Ensure correct timing for interpretation. Trap: Drawing right after dose and ‘seeing toxicity’.

cards.title: SSRI start: delayed effect
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Antidepressant benefit can take weeks.
Takeaway: Teach adherence; monitor suicide risk early. Trap: Stopping after 3 days because ‘no change’.

cards.title: Serotonin syndrome vs NMS
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SS is hyperreflexia/clonus; NMS is lead-pipe rigidity.
Takeaway: Different triggers; both are emergencies. Trap: Treating SS with more antipsychotic.

modules.title: 3. Pharmacology I: High-Yield Med Classes

modules.moduleDescription: High‑yield med safety: when to HOLD a drug, key labs/vitals to check, toxicity signs, antidotes, interactions, and high‑alert meds (NCLEX-style traps).

cards.title: Hold metoprolol: which vital sign?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Check apical pulse before beta‑blockers.
Takeaway/Trap: Hold if HR <60 (or per order); trap: BP low alone isn’t the classic hold parameter.

cards.title: Hold lisinopril: what lab matters?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ACE inhibitors can increase potassium.
Takeaway/Trap: Hold/notify if K+ elevated; trap: low Na+ is not the key ACE hold lab.

cards.title: ACE inhibitor first-dose risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ACE inhibitors can cause first‑dose hypotension.
Takeaway/Trap: Start low, monitor BP; trap: give at bedtime doesn’t replace monitoring.

cards.title: Statin timing clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Shorter‑acting statins work best when cholesterol synthesis peaks.
Takeaway/Trap: Give in the evening for many statins; trap: atorvastatin/rosuvastatin can be any time.

cards.title: Statin red flag symptom
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Statins can cause myopathy/rhabdo.
Takeaway/Trap: Report muscle pain/weakness + dark urine; trap: mild headache isn’t the big danger.

cards.title: Warfarin antidote
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Vitamin K reverses warfarin effect.
Takeaway/Trap: Give phytonadione for high INR/bleeding; trap: protamine is for heparin.

cards.title: Heparin antidote
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protamine sulfate reverses heparin.
Takeaway/Trap: Use protamine for heparin overdose; trap: vitamin K won’t fix heparin.

cards.title: Heparin monitoring lab
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Unfractionated heparin is titrated by coag labs.
Takeaway/Trap: Monitor aPTT (or anti‑Xa protocol); trap: INR is warfarin.

cards.title: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: HIT is immune platelet activation with thrombosis risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Stop heparin if platelets drop; trap: don’t give more heparin to “treat” clot.

cards.title: DOAC safety check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Many DOACs depend on renal clearance.
Takeaway/Trap: Assess kidney function; trap: routine INR checks aren’t used for DOAC dosing.

cards.title: Aspirin + bleeding risk combo
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Antiplatelets + anticoagulants raise bleeding risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Watch bruising, GI bleed; trap: “one is OTC so it’s safe” is wrong.

cards.title: NSAID kidney trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: NSAIDs reduce renal perfusion.
Takeaway/Trap: Avoid in CKD/dehydration; trap: normal urine output today doesn’t guarantee safety.

cards.title: NSAID GI protection
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: NSAIDs can cause ulcers/bleeding.
Takeaway/Trap: Take with food, consider PPI if ordered; trap: enteric‑coated ≠ no GI risk.

cards.title: Acetaminophen max risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Acetaminophen is hepatotoxic at high doses.
Takeaway/Trap: Don’t exceed daily max (often 4 g; lower if liver disease); trap: multiple combo meds add up.

cards.title: Metformin big contraindication
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Metformin risk: lactic acidosis with poor perfusion/renal issues.
Takeaway/Trap: Hold for IV contrast and in severe renal impairment; trap: “take extra with high sugar” is wrong.

cards.title: Insulin onset vs meal
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rapid‑acting insulin must match food intake.
Takeaway/Trap: Give when meal is present/ready; trap: giving then tray delays → hypoglycemia.

cards.title: Hypoglycemia first action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Low glucose is an immediate safety priority.
Takeaway/Trap: Give fast carbs if conscious; IV dextrose/glucagon if not; trap: don’t give insulin.

cards.title: Long-acting insulin rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Basal insulin covers baseline needs, not meals.
Takeaway/Trap: Do not mix glargine/detemir; trap: holding basal “because NPO” can cause hyperglycemia.

cards.title: Digoxin toxicity early sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Digoxin has narrow therapeutic index.
Takeaway/Trap: N/V, anorexia, bradycardia, vision changes; trap: normal BP doesn’t rule out toxicity.

cards.title: Digoxin hold parameter
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Check apical pulse before digoxin.
Takeaway/Trap: Hold if HR <60 (adult) and notify; trap: radial pulse is less reliable.

cards.title: Digoxin + low K+ danger
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hypokalemia increases digoxin toxicity.
Takeaway/Trap: Correct K+; trap: giving digoxin when K+ low is unsafe.

cards.title: Nitroglycerin contraindication combo
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Nitrates + PDE5 inhibitors can crash BP.
Takeaway/Trap: No sildenafil/tadalafil within timeframe; trap: “it was last week” still needs timing check.

cards.title: Nitro headache teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Vasodilation causes headaches.
Takeaway/Trap: Common effect; manage with mild analgesic; trap: stop med without provider direction.

cards.title: Opioid priority assessment
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Opioids depress respiration.
Takeaway/Trap: RR and sedation level before dose; trap: pain score alone isn’t enough.

cards.title: Naloxone teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Naloxone reverses opioids briefly.
Takeaway/Trap: Monitor for re‑sedation; trap: “one dose fixes it” is wrong.

cards.title: Benzodiazepine reversal
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Flumazenil can reverse benzos but has risks.
Takeaway/Trap: Use cautiously; trap: can precipitate seizures in chronic benzo users.

cards.title: Serotonin syndrome triad
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Too much serotonin → autonomic + neuro + GI signs.
Takeaway/Trap: Agitation, hyperreflexia, diaphoresis, diarrhea; trap: treat as emergency, not “flu.”

cards.title: MAOI food interaction
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: MAOIs + tyramine can cause hypertensive crisis.
Takeaway/Trap: Avoid aged cheeses/cured meats; trap: “a little is fine” is unsafe.

cards.title: SSRI bleeding interaction
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SSRIs can increase bleeding risk, esp with NSAIDs/anticoags.
Takeaway/Trap: Assess bruising/GI bleed; trap: “only affects mood” is wrong.

cards.title: Lithium toxicity trigger
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Lithium levels rise with dehydration/low Na+.
Takeaway/Trap: Hydrate, maintain salt; trap: diuretics and NSAIDs can increase lithium.

cards.title: Lithium lab monitoring
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Lithium has narrow therapeutic index.
Takeaway/Trap: Check serum levels and kidney/thyroid; trap: symptoms can appear before you “feel” sick.

cards.title: Antipsychotic NMS red flag
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is life‑threatening.
Takeaway/Trap: Fever, rigidity, altered mental status; trap: don’t give more antipsychotic.

cards.title: QT prolongation med safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some meds prolong QT and risk torsades.
Takeaway/Trap: Review ECG, electrolytes; trap: giving QT‑prolongers with low K/Mg is dangerous.

cards.title: Albuterol side effect clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Beta‑agonists stimulate heart.
Takeaway/Trap: Tremor, tachycardia expected; trap: bradycardia is not typical.

cards.title: Steroid taper rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Systemic steroids need taper if long-term.
Takeaway/Trap: Don’t stop abruptly; trap: sudden stop → adrenal crisis.

cards.title: Inhaled steroid teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Inhaled steroids can cause oral candidiasis.
Takeaway/Trap: Rinse mouth after use; trap: using as rescue med is wrong.

cards.title: Theophylline toxicity sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Theophylline is narrow therapeutic index.
Takeaway/Trap: N/V, seizures, dysrhythmias; trap: caffeine increases side effects.

cards.title: Antibiotic: anaphylaxis priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Severe allergy can occur with any antibiotic.
Takeaway/Trap: Stop infusion, maintain airway, give epi per protocol; trap: “just slow the rate” is wrong.

cards.title: Antibiotic: finish the course
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Incomplete antibiotics promote resistance/relapse.
Takeaway/Trap: Take full prescribed duration; trap: stopping when “feels better” is wrong.

cards.title: Vancomycin infusion reaction
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rapid vanco can cause Red Man syndrome.
Takeaway/Trap: Infuse slowly, monitor; trap: it’s not always IgE allergy but still needs action.

cards.title: Aminoglycoside monitoring
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Aminoglycosides are oto/nephrotoxic.
Takeaway/Trap: Monitor hearing and creatinine; trap: “normal baseline” doesn’t prevent toxicity.

cards.title: Fluoroquinolone tendon risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Fluoroquinolones can cause tendon rupture.
Takeaway/Trap: Report tendon pain; trap: athletes still at risk.

cards.title: Tetracycline chelation trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tetracyclines bind calcium/iron.
Takeaway/Trap: Separate from dairy/antacids; trap: taking with milk decreases absorption.

cards.title: Oral contraceptive antibiotic myth check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some antibiotics reduce OCP effectiveness.
Takeaway/Trap: Use backup if instructed (esp rifampin); trap: assume “no interaction” without checking.

cards.title: Rifampin body fluid color
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rifampin can discolor secretions.
Takeaway/Trap: Orange urine/tears is expected; trap: contact lenses may stain.

cards.title: C. diff risk after antibiotics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Broad antibiotics can cause C. diff diarrhea.
Takeaway/Trap: Report watery diarrhea; trap: antidiarrheals can worsen severe cases.

cards.title: Insulin + beta-blocker trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Beta‑blockers mask hypoglycemia symptoms.
Takeaway/Trap: Teach to monitor glucose; trap: absence of tremor/palpitations ≠ safe.

cards.title: Diuretic: loop K+ effect
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Loop diuretics waste potassium.
Takeaway/Trap: Monitor K+; trap: muscle cramps can be hypokalemia sign.

cards.title: Spironolactone K+ effect
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: K‑sparing diuretics raise potassium.
Takeaway/Trap: Avoid salt substitutes; trap: “it’s a diuretic so K drops” is wrong.

cards.title: Diuretic: daily weights
cards.cardDescription:
