Rule: Weights best indicator of fluid change.
Takeaway/Trap: Same time, same scale; trap: I&O alone can miss third spacing.

cards.title: ACE/ARB pregnancy contraindication
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ACE/ARBs are teratogenic.
Takeaway/Trap: Avoid in pregnancy; trap: stop and notify provider immediately.

cards.title: Isotretinoin pregnancy rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Isotretinoin causes severe birth defects.
Takeaway/Trap: Two forms of contraception/regular tests; trap: “low dose is safe” is false.

cards.title: Retinoid side effect teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Isotretinoin dries tissues.
Takeaway/Trap: Use moisturizer, avoid wax/peels; trap: donate blood is restricted during/after therapy.

cards.title: Methotrexate safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Methotrexate is teratogenic/immunosuppressive.
Takeaway/Trap: Monitor CBC/LFTs; trap: weekly dosing—daily is a lethal error.

cards.title: Heparin in pregnancy clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Heparin is often preferred anticoagulant in pregnancy.
Takeaway/Trap: It doesn’t cross placenta; trap: warfarin is teratogenic.

cards.title: Live vaccines immunosuppression trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Immunosuppressed patients should avoid live vaccines.
Takeaway/Trap: Check med list (steroids, biologics); trap: “vaccines are always safe” is wrong.

cards.title: Warfarin dietary consistency
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Vitamin K intake affects INR.
Takeaway/Trap: Keep greens consistent; trap: sudden “healthy salad week” can lower INR.

cards.title: Grapefruit interaction
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Grapefruit inhibits CYP3A4 for many drugs.
Takeaway/Trap: Avoid with certain statins/CCBs; trap: grapefruit juice counts.

cards.title: Alcohol + acetaminophen
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Alcohol increases liver toxicity risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Limit/avoid; trap: ‘one extra dose’ can be dangerous in heavy drinkers.

cards.title: Herb: St. John’s wort
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: St. John’s wort induces enzymes and interacts widely.
Takeaway/Trap: Can reduce OCP/warfarin levels; trap: ‘natural’ ≠ safe.

cards.title: High-alert med: insulin
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Insulin errors can be fatal.
Takeaway/Trap: Independent double-check, no trailing zeros; trap: U-100 vs U-500 confusion.

cards.title: High-alert med: heparin
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Heparin dosing errors cause bleeding.
Takeaway/Trap: Use pump, verify concentration; trap: flush vs infusion strengths differ.

cards.title: High-alert med: potassium IV
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: IV potassium must be diluted and infused slowly.
Takeaway/Trap: Never IV push; trap: giving undiluted K+ can cause arrest.

cards.title: Potassium infusion pain clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: K+ can irritate veins.
Takeaway/Trap: Use larger vein, dilute; trap: slowing too much may delay correction in severe cases.

cards.title: Calcium channel blocker hold
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Non‑DHP CCBs can lower HR.
Takeaway/Trap: Check HR/BP; trap: edema is common effect, not allergy.

cards.title: Beta-blocker asthma trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Nonselective beta‑blockers can worsen bronchospasm.
Takeaway/Trap: Assess respiratory history; trap: giving propranolol in asthma can be risky.

cards.title: Clonidine rebound
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stopping clonidine abruptly can cause rebound HTN.
Takeaway/Trap: Taper; trap: missing doses can spike BP.

cards.title: Thiazide hyperglycemia
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Thiazides can raise glucose and uric acid.
Takeaway/Trap: Watch diabetics/gout; trap: ‘only affects BP’ is wrong.

cards.title: Opioid constipation prevention
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Constipation is expected with opioids.
Takeaway/Trap: Start stool softener/fluids; trap: waiting until severe constipation makes it harder.

cards.title: Chemo extravasation priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Vesicant chemo can damage tissue.
Takeaway/Trap: Stop infusion, leave needle, follow antidote protocol; trap: flushing the line spreads injury.

cards.title: PICC/central line med safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Irritants/vesicants require central access.
Takeaway/Trap: Verify line patency; trap: don’t give vesicants through fragile peripheral vein.

cards.title: IV compatibility check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some meds precipitate when mixed.
Takeaway/Trap: Use compatibility chart; trap: ‘clear in tubing’ doesn’t guarantee compatibility.

cards.title: Crush/not crush rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Extended‑release/enteric-coated meds shouldn’t be crushed.
Takeaway/Trap: Ask pharmacy; trap: crushing ER can cause dose dumping.

cards.title: Sublingual nitro handling
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SL meds need dry mouth and no swallowing.
Takeaway/Trap: Let dissolve; trap: swallowing reduces effect.

cards.title: Insulin storage
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Insulin potency declines with heat/freezing.
Takeaway/Trap: Refrigerate unopened; trap: don’t store in hot car.

cards.title: Expired meds trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Many meds lose potency after expiration.
Takeaway/Trap: Replace promptly; trap: ‘it still works’ is not reliable.

cards.title: Allergy vs side effect
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: True allergy involves immune reaction (hives, swelling, anaphylaxis).
Takeaway/Trap: Nausea isn’t allergy; trap: documenting side effect as allergy limits options.

cards.title: Penicillin cross-reactivity
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some beta‑lactams cross-react.
Takeaway/Trap: Assess reaction type; trap: mild GI upset ≠ true PCN allergy.

cards.title: Contrast + metformin safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Metformin plus contrast can increase lactic acidosis risk if kidneys injured.
Takeaway/Trap: Hold per protocol and recheck renal function; trap: restarting same day may be unsafe.

cards.title: Ototoxic meds list cue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Loop diuretics, aminoglycosides can be ototoxic.
Takeaway/Trap: Report tinnitus/hearing loss; trap: waiting for next visit can cause permanent loss.

cards.title: Nephrotoxic combo trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: NSAIDs + ACE/ARB + diuretic can injure kidneys.
Takeaway/Trap: Monitor creatinine, hydration; trap: ‘each is common’ doesn’t mean safe together.

cards.title: Lab: INR meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: INR monitors warfarin effect.
Takeaway/Trap: High INR → bleeding risk; trap: doesn’t guide heparin titration.

cards.title: Lab: aPTT meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: aPTT monitors unfractionated heparin.
Takeaway/Trap: Target range per protocol; trap: platelet count matters too (HIT).

cards.title: Lab: trough vs peak
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some drugs require level timing.
Takeaway/Trap: Trough just before dose; trap: wrong timing gives misleading “normal” values.

cards.title: Gentamicin trough purpose
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: High trough increases toxicity risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Hold/adjust if elevated; trap: ‘normal peak’ doesn’t prevent toxicity.

cards.title: Vancomycin levels
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Vanco dosing often guided by levels/renal function.
Takeaway/Trap: Draw at correct time; trap: kidney decline needs dose adjustment.

cards.title: Insulin sliding scale trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sliding scale alone is reactive.
Takeaway/Trap: Combine with basal/meal plan as ordered; trap: chasing highs causes swings.

cards.title: Anticoagulant injection teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SQ anticoagulants need correct technique.
Takeaway/Trap: Don’t expel air bubble (enoxaparin), don’t massage; trap: rubbing increases bruising.

cards.title: Enoxaparin injection site
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rotate abdominal sites.
Takeaway/Trap: Stay 2 inches from umbilicus; trap: IM injection increases bleeding.

cards.title: Aspirin before surgery
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Antiplatelets increase bleeding risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Follow surgeon/provider instructions; trap: stopping abruptly without guidance can risk clot.

cards.title: PPI long-term risk clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Long-term PPIs can affect minerals/infection risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Monitor Mg/B12 as appropriate; trap: “no side effects” is wrong.

cards.title: Antacid timing trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Antacids can block absorption of other meds.
Takeaway/Trap: Separate by 1–2 hours; trap: taking all together reduces efficacy.

cards.title: Iron supplement teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Iron best absorbed on empty stomach but causes GI upset.
Takeaway/Trap: Take with vitamin C; trap: dairy/antacids reduce absorption.

cards.title: Iron black stool
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Iron can darken stools.
Takeaway/Trap: Expected; trap: tarry stool with symptoms could be GI bleed—assess context.

cards.title: Levothyroxine timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Thyroid hormone needs consistent absorption.
Takeaway/Trap: Take AM, empty stomach, separate from iron/calcium; trap: taking with breakfast reduces effect.

cards.title: Thyroid med overreplacement sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Too much thyroid hormone causes hyperthyroid symptoms.
Takeaway/Trap: Palpitations, weight loss, insomnia; trap: don’t increase dose for fatigue without labs.

cards.title: Insulin vs oral hypoglycemics in NPO
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: NPO status changes med plan.
Takeaway/Trap: Hold many oral agents; basal insulin may continue; trap: treating NPO like ‘no diabetes’ is wrong.

cards.title: Sulfonylurea hypoglycemia risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sulfonylureas can cause prolonged hypoglycemia.
Takeaway/Trap: Monitor glucose and meals; trap: long-acting agents can drop sugar overnight.

cards.title: Antiemetic sedation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some antiemetics sedate (e.g., promethazine).
Takeaway/Trap: Fall precautions; trap: giving before ambulation increases fall risk.

cards.title: Anticholinergic effects
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Anticholinergics cause dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation.
Takeaway/Trap: Use caution in BPH/elderly; trap: confusion can be a side effect, not dementia.

cards.title: Elderly polypharmacy risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Older adults have altered metabolism and higher fall risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Start low/go slow; trap: “home dose” may be too high in acute illness.

cards.title: Renal dosing rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Many drugs need dose reduction in renal impairment.
Takeaway/Trap: Check creatinine/eGFR; trap: ‘normal urine’ doesn’t equal normal clearance.

cards.title: Hepatic dosing rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Liver disease affects drug metabolism.
Takeaway/Trap: Watch LFTs and bleeding risk; trap: sedatives/opioids can accumulate.

cards.title: Pregnancy med principle
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assume meds may affect fetus unless known safe.
Takeaway/Trap: Verify pregnancy status; trap: first trimester is highest teratogenic risk.

cards.title: Breastfeeding med principle
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Many meds enter breast milk.
Takeaway/Trap: Check lactation safety; trap: “topical is always safe” is not always true.

cards.title: Photo-sensitivity meds
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some meds cause photosensitivity (tetracyclines, sulfonamides).
Takeaway/Trap: Use sunscreen/cover; trap: tanning beds increase burns.

cards.title: Sun + retinoids trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Retinoids increase sun sensitivity and skin fragility.
Takeaway/Trap: Avoid intense sun; trap: waxing/laser can tear skin.

cards.title: Opiate + alcohol/benzo combo
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: CNS depressants together can cause respiratory failure.
Takeaway/Trap: Avoid mixing; trap: ‘different meds’ doesn’t mean safe.

cards.title: Patient-controlled analgesia safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: PCA is for the patient only.
Takeaway/Trap: Family must not press button; trap: “helping” can overdose.

cards.title: Transdermal patch safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Patches deliver long-acting medication through skin.
Takeaway/Trap: Remove old patch before applying new; trap: heat increases absorption.

cards.title: Fentanyl patch trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Fentanyl patches are for opioid-tolerant chronic pain.
Takeaway/Trap: Not for acute pain; trap: cutting patch alters dose delivery.

cards.title: Eye drops: order matters
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Multiple eye meds need spacing.
Takeaway/Trap: Wait ~5 minutes between drops; trap: touching tip contaminates.

cards.title: Ear drops: adult vs child angle
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Position affects delivery.
Takeaway/Trap: Adults: up/back; kids <3: down/back; trap: wrong angle reduces effectiveness.

cards.title: Oxygen + meds safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some meds depress respiration; oxygen doesn’t fix hypoventilation.
Takeaway/Trap: Treat cause and monitor; trap: just turning up O2 can hide respiratory failure.

cards.title: Anaphylaxis first-line med
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Epinephrine IM is first-line for anaphylaxis.
Takeaway/Trap: Airway + epi early; trap: antihistamines are adjunct, not first.

cards.title: Epi autoinjector teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Epi must be accessible and used promptly.
Takeaway/Trap: Hold in place per device instructions; trap: injecting thumb causes ischemia.

modules.title: 4. Pharmacology II: Safety & Interactions

modules.moduleDescription: Core med-math for NCLEX: unit conversions, tablets/liquids, IV rates, weight-based dosing, reconstitution, and safety rounding with common traps.

cards.title: Leading zero vs trailing zero
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use a leading zero for doses <1; never use trailing zeros.
Takeaway/Trap: Write 0.5 mg (not .5); write 5 mg (not 5.0) to prevent 10× errors.

cards.title: mL to L conversion
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: 1 L = 1000 mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: move decimal 3 places (250 mL = 0.25 L).

cards.title: kg from lb quick rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: kg = lb ÷ 2.2.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: multiplying by 2.2 gives the wrong direction (overdoses).

cards.title: mg to g conversion
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: 1 g = 1000 mg.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: 0.25 g = 250 mg (not 25 mg).

cards.title: mcg to mg conversion
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: 1 mg = 1000 mcg.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: 400 mcg = 0.4 mg (not 4 mg).

cards.title: Dimensional analysis anchor
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Keep units in fractions so they cancel.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: if units don’t cancel, your setup is wrong.

cards.title: Tablet dose formula
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tablets to give = (desired ÷ have) × quantity.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘have’ is per tablet strength, not total in bottle.

cards.title: Liquid dose formula
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: mL to give = (desired ÷ have) × mL on hand.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: match units first (mg with mg, not mg with g).

cards.title: Reconstitution: final concentration
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: After reconstitution, use the label’s concentration (e.g., mg/mL).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: using powder amount instead of final mg/mL gives wrong dose.

cards.title: Drop factor meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: gtt/mL is set-specific, not universal.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: using 20 gtt/mL when tubing is 15 gtt/mL changes rate.

cards.title: Gravity IV gtt/min
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: gtt/min = (mL/hr × gtt/mL) ÷ 60.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: forgetting ÷60 inflates rate 60×.

cards.title: Pump IV mL/hr
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: For pumps, calculate in mL/hr.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t give gtt/min when order asks mL/hr.

cards.title: Time conversion trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: 60 min/hr; 24 hr/day.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: 1.5 hr = 90 min (not 150).

cards.title: Half-life intuition
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: After 1 half-life, 50% remains; after 2, 25%.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: half-life is multiplicative, not subtractive.

cards.title: Safe dose check step
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Compare ordered dose with safe range before giving.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘it’s ordered’ doesn’t mean it’s safe—verify and call.

cards.title: Convert 154 lb to kg
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Divide pounds by 2.2.
Takeaway/Trap: 154 ÷ 2.2 = 70 kg; trap: rounding too early changes mg/kg results.

cards.title: Dose per kg setup
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Ordered mg/kg × weight (kg) = total mg.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: using lb instead of kg gives 2.2× overdose.

cards.title: Round when?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Round only at the end unless policy says otherwise.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: early rounding can shift answer beyond safe limits.

cards.title: mL/hr from volume & time
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: mL/hr = total mL ÷ hours.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: if time is minutes, convert to hours first.

cards.title: Minutes to hours
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: hours = minutes ÷ 60.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: 30 min = 0.5 hr (not 0.30 hr).

cards.title: gtt/min quick check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If gtt/min is huge, re-check ÷60 and drop factor.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: many errors are missing the ÷60.

cards.title: Order: 0.25 g; supply: 125 mg/tab
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Convert 0.25 g to 250 mg first.
Takeaway/Trap: 250 ÷ 125 = 2 tablets; trap: forgetting g→mg gives 0.2 tab.

cards.title: Order: 15 mg; supply: 10 mg/5 mL
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use desired/have × 5 mL.
Takeaway/Trap: (15/10)×5 = 7.5 mL; trap: swapping desired/have flips dose.

cards.title: Order: 0.4 mg; supply: 200 mcg/tab
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Convert 0.4 mg to 400 mcg.
Takeaway/Trap: 400 ÷ 200 = 2 tabs; trap: 0.4 mg ≠ 40 mcg.

cards.title: Reconstitution label
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If label says 1 g + 9.6 mL → 100 mg/mL, use 100 mg/mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: using 1 g/10 mL = 100 mg/mL is fine ONLY if final volume is 10 mL.

cards.title: IV order: 1000 mL over 8 hr
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: mL/hr = 1000/8.
Takeaway/Trap: 125 mL/hr; trap: dividing by 8 minutes is wrong.

cards.title: Gravity IV: 125 mL/hr, 15 gtt/mL
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: gtt/min = (125×15)/60.
Takeaway/Trap: 31 gtt/min (rounded); trap: not rounding per policy.

cards.title: Microdrip set
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Microdrip is often 60 gtt/mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: with 60 gtt/mL, gtt/min ≈ mL/hr (same number).

cards.title: Order: 500 mL over 30 min
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Convert 30 min to 0.5 hr.
Takeaway/Trap: mL/hr = 500/0.5 = 1000 mL/hr; trap: forgetting 0.5.

cards.title: Order: 2 L over 24 hr
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Convert 2 L to 2000 mL.
Takeaway/Trap: 2000/24 ≈ 83 mL/hr; trap: leaving liters in numerator.

cards.title: Insulin units rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Insulin is measured in units, not mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: never convert units to mg—use U-100 concentration only when needed.

cards.title: Heparin drip concentration
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use bag label (units/mL) to convert units/hr → mL/hr.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: units and mL must be linked by concentration.

cards.title: Weight-based heparin bolus
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Bolus = units/kg × kg.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: cap the bolus if protocol has a max.

cards.title: Pediatric safe range check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Calculate min and max safe dose before comparing to order.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: comparing order to only one boundary misses overdoses.

cards.title: Order: 25 mcg; supply: 0.1 mg/mL
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Convert 0.1 mg to 100 mcg per mL.
Takeaway/Trap: 25 mcg = 0.25 mL; trap: mg↔mcg mismatch.

cards.title: Order: 1:1000 epi meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: 1:1000 = 1 g in 1000 mL = 1 mg/mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t confuse with 1:10,000 (0.1 mg/mL).

cards.title: Percent solutions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: 1% = 1 g/100 mL = 10 mg/mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: 2% lidocaine = 20 mg/mL (double 1%).

cards.title: mEq vs mg
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: mEq depends on valence and molecular weight.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: do not convert mEq to mg without a reference table.

cards.title: IV piggyback time
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If 100 mL over 30 min, rate = 200 mL/hr.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: 30 min is half an hour.

cards.title: Drip rate sanity
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Adult maintenance fluids rarely exceed a few hundred mL/hr.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: 1500 mL/hr should trigger re-check.

cards.title: Dose in mg from concentration
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: mg = mL × (mg/mL).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: dividing when you should multiply flips the dose.

cards.title: mL from mg/mL
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: mL = desired mg ÷ (mg/mL).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: desired mg must match mg units.

cards.title: Unit cancellation test
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Write units at every step to catch mistakes.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘numbers only’ hides errors.

cards.title: Decimal placement check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Move decimal 3 places for ×/÷1000.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: 0.05 g = 50 mg, not 5 mg.

cards.title: Rounding for tablets
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If tablets can’t be split, round to available form.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t round 1.6 tabs to 2 unless splitting is allowed.

cards.title: Rounding for insulin syringes
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Round to the nearest unit if syringe allows.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: some pens dose in 1-unit or 2-unit increments.

cards.title: Primary IV with titration
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: For titrated meds, changes are by mL/hr or units/min per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t ‘guess’—use concentration.

cards.title: Flow rate with microdrip
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: With 60 gtt/mL, gtt/min equals mL/hr.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: only true for 60 gtt/mL sets.

cards.title: Safe pediatric mg/kg/day
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Total daily dose may be split; track totals.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: forgetting multiple daily doses can exceed max/day.

cards.title: Body surface area dosing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some chemo uses mg/m² based on BSA.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t substitute kg for m² calculations.

cards.title: Two-step conversions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Do one conversion at a time (e.g., g→mg then mg→mL).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: skipping steps increases unit errors.

cards.title: Concentration after dilution
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: New mg/mL = total mg ÷ total mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: adding diluent changes concentration.

cards.title: IV push rate rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some meds must be given slowly over minutes.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: dose calc is right but speed can still harm.

cards.title: Tuberculin syringe
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: TB syringe is 1 mL with 0.01 increments.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: reading 0.1 as 1.0 causes 10× error.

cards.title: Insulin syringe
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Insulin syringe is in units, not mL markings.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: never draw insulin with a TB syringe unless instructed.

cards.title: Oral syringe vs spoon
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use an oral syringe for accuracy.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: household teaspoons are inaccurate.

cards.title: Drop vs mL confusion
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Drops are not a standard volume unless drop factor given.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘20 drops = 1 mL’ is not universal.

cards.title: High-alert double-check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Independent verification for insulin/heparin/chemo.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘I already checked’ doesn’t replace independent check.

cards.title: Dose range includes weight?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use current documented weight for mg/kg.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: using ‘estimated’ weight can be unsafe.

cards.title: Convert ounces to mL (common)
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: 1 oz ≈ 30 mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: for strict med dosing, follow facility conversion chart.

cards.title: Household teaspoon trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: 1 tsp = 5 mL, 1 Tbsp = 15 mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: mixing tsp/Tbsp triples the dose.

cards.title: Apothecary trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid apothecary system; convert to metric.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘gr’ (grain) varies—use approved reference.

cards.title: Infusion completion time
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: time (hr) = total mL ÷ mL/hr.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: if result is >24 hr, re-check inputs.

cards.title: Order per minute
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Convert per minute to per hour if pump uses hr.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: multiplying by 60 is required.

cards.title: Titration per kg per min
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: mcg/kg/min × kg = mcg/min.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: then convert mcg/min to mg/hr only if needed.

cards.title: When to call provider on calc
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If ordered dose exceeds safe range or seems extreme.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t administer then ‘report later’.

cards.title: ‘Per dose’ vs ‘per day’
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Clarify whether safe range is per dose or per day.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: confusing these can double or triple dosing.

cards.title: Multiple concentrations exist
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Always verify concentration on hand (e.g., morphine 2 vs 4 mg/mL).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: using the ‘usual’ concentration causes wrong mL.

cards.title: Concentration units must match
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: mg/mL cannot be used with mcg without converting.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: skipping conversion gives 1000× errors.

cards.title: Split tablets safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Only split if scored and policy allows.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ER/enteric-coated tablets should not be split.

cards.title: Calculate first, then compare
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Do the math first, then assess plausibility.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: letting ‘expected’ answer bias your math hides errors.

cards.title: Peds: weight in kg only
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Peds dosing is always in kg in calculations.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: charting weight in lb then dosing in kg causes mismatch.

cards.title: IV rate with secondary tubing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Secondary/primary rates differ; ensure correct channel.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: setting piggyback rate on primary channel can over-infuse.

cards.title: mEq KCl common vial trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: KCl is often labeled in mEq per mL (e.g., 2 mEq/mL).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t treat mEq like mg; use label directly.

cards.title: IV rate: 250 mL over 2.5 hr
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: mL/hr = 250 ÷ 2.5.
Takeaway/Trap: 100 mL/hr; trap: 2.5 hr = 2 hr 30 min.

cards.title: IV rate: 75 mL over 45 min
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Convert 45 min to 0.75 hr.
Takeaway/Trap: Rate = 100 mL/hr; trap: 45 min is not 0.45 hr.

cards.title: mcg/min to mg/hr
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Multiply by 60 then divide by 1000 (mcg→mg).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: missing either step gives 60× or 1000× error.

cards.title: mg/hr to mL/hr
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: mL/hr = mg/hr ÷ (mg/mL).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ensure mg/mL is the actual bag concentration.

cards.title: Weight-based: 5 mg/kg for 18 kg
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Total = 5×18 mg.
Takeaway/Trap: 90 mg; trap: don’t round 18 kg to 20 unless allowed.

cards.title: Safe range example logic
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If safe is 2–4 mg/kg and dose is 5 mg/kg → unsafe.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘close enough’ is not acceptable.

cards.title: Reconstitution volume vs displacement
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some powders displace volume; final mL may not equal added diluent.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: use manufacturer’s stated final concentration.

cards.title: Percent to mg/mL shortcut
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: 1% = 10 mg/mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: 0.5% = 5 mg/mL (half of 1%).

cards.title: Units in insulin U-100
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: U-100 = 100 units per mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: 25 units = 0.25 mL, but draw by units markings.

cards.title: TB syringe reading 0.36 mL
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Each small line is 0.01 mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: reading 0.36 as 0.6 is a common error.

cards.title: Oral suspension shake
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Suspensions must be shaken before measuring.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: not shaking changes mg per mL delivered.

cards.title: Liquid label: per 5 mL
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Many pediatric meds list strength per 5 mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treating it as per 1 mL overdoses 5×.

cards.title: Order: 2.5 mL; syringe in mL
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use oral syringe with 0.1 mL marks.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: kitchen spoon cannot measure 2.5 mL accurately.

cards.title: Drip set change
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Different tubing can change gtt/mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: recalibrate gtt/min when tubing changes.

cards.title: IV bolus over minutes
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: mL/hr = (mL ÷ minutes) × 60.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: forgetting ×60 under-infuses by 60×.

cards.title: Convert mg to mcg
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Multiply mg by 1000.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: 0.2 mg = 200 mcg (not 20 mcg).

cards.title: Convert L to mL
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Multiply liters by 1000.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: 1.2 L = 1200 mL (not 12,000).

cards.title: Convert mg to g
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Divide mg by 1000.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: 750 mg = 0.75 g (not 7.5 g).

cards.title: Convert mL to tsp
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: 1 tsp = 5 mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: 10 mL = 2 tsp.

cards.title: Convert mL to tbsp
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: 1 Tbsp = 15 mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: 30 mL = 2 Tbsp.

cards.title: Order frequency trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: q6h = 4 doses/day.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: q8h = 3/day; don’t assume 2/day.

cards.title: IV insulin drip units/hr
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pump often in mL/hr, order in units/hr.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: convert using units/mL from bag label.

cards.title: Heparin: 25,000 units in 250 mL
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Concentration = 100 units/mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: if order is 1200 units/hr → 12 mL/hr.

cards.title: Titration per protocol
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use titration table; don’t freehand math under stress.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: wrong table row can double the dose.

cards.title: Weight changes matter
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use most current weight for drips.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: using admission weight after diuresis misdoses.

cards.title: ‘mg/kg/min’ conversion step
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Compute mg/kg/min → mg/min → mg/hr.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: skipping to mg/hr without ×60 is wrong.

cards.title: Peds: max single dose
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Many meds have max per dose and per day.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: meeting mg/kg but exceeding max is still unsafe.

cards.title: Check concentration on MAR
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: MAR may list different concentration than pharmacy label.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: trust the actual pharmacy label on the product.

modules.title: 5. Dosage Calculations

modules.moduleDescription: High-yield adult health for NCLEX focused on airway, breathing, circulation: asthma/COPD, pneumonia/PE, heart failure/MI, dysrhythmias, oxygen therapy, ABGs, chest tubes, and priority nursing actions (with classic traps).

cards.title: ABC priority shortcut
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Airway and breathing problems come before circulation unless severe bleeding/shock.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘chest pain’ isn’t first if the airway is threatened.

cards.title: Resp distress first action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess and support oxygenation/ventilation immediately.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: calling provider before applying O2/positioning delays care.

cards.title: Tripod position meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tripod posture suggests increased work of breathing.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t lay flat; sit up and apply O2.

cards.title: Pursed-lip breathing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prolongs exhalation and reduces air trapping in COPD.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: hyperventilating fast worsens dyspnea.

cards.title: Accessory muscle use
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use of accessory muscles indicates respiratory fatigue.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘talking in full sentences’ is a better sign than SpO2 alone.

cards.title: Silent chest in asthma
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: No wheeze with severe asthma can mean minimal airflow.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘wheezing stopped’ is NOT improvement if still distressed.

cards.title: Peak flow red zone
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Very low peak flow signals severe asthma exacerbation.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t wait for labs—treat and escalate quickly.

cards.title: Asthma rescue vs control
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SABA (albuterol) is rescue; inhaled steroids are control.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: using steroid inhaler for sudden SOB won’t help fast.

cards.title: COPD O2 target
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: COPD often targets SpO2 ~88–92% per orders.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: cranking O2 to 100% without order can worsen CO2 retention in some.

cards.title: CO2 retainer clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Chronic COPD may have high CO2 with compensated pH.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: pH may look ‘near normal’ while CO2 is high.

cards.title: ABG: respiratory acidosis
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: High CO2 with low pH suggests hypoventilation.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treating acidosis with bicarbonate without fixing ventilation misses cause.

cards.title: ABG: respiratory alkalosis
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Low CO2 with high pH suggests hyperventilation.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: anxiety can cause it; don’t give opioids to ‘calm’ without assessment.

cards.title: ABG: metabolic acidosis
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Low HCO3- with low pH suggests metabolic acidosis.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: Kussmaul respirations are compensation—don’t suppress breathing.

cards.title: ABG: metabolic alkalosis
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: High HCO3- with high pH suggests metabolic alkalosis.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: vomiting/diuretics can cause; watch hypokalemia.

cards.title: Pulse ox limitation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SpO2 doesn’t show ventilation/CO2 status.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: a patient can be ‘pink’ but retaining CO2 (need ABG/ETCO2).

cards.title: O2 delivery: nasal cannula
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Low-flow oxygen for mild/moderate needs.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: mouth breathing doesn’t ‘cancel’ nasal cannula benefit.

cards.title: O2 delivery: nonrebreather
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: High FiO2 for severe hypoxia, keep reservoir inflated.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: empty bag = wrong setup/flow too low.

cards.title: Humidification rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Humidify higher flows or prolonged O2 per policy.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: dry mucosa increases bleeding and discomfort.

cards.title: Suctioning priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pre-oxygenate and limit suction time.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: prolonged suctioning causes hypoxia/bradycardia.

cards.title: COPD exacerbation basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Bronchodilators + steroids + controlled O2 are common first steps.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: antibiotics only if infection suspected.

cards.title: COPD barrel chest
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hyperinflation is common in COPD.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: decreased breath sounds can be baseline; look at work of breathing.

cards.title: Pneumonia assessment
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Crackles, fever, cough, and increased sputum suggest pneumonia.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: elderly may have confusion more than fever.

cards.title: Pneumonia: best sample timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Collect sputum culture before antibiotics when possible.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: after antibiotics reduces culture accuracy.

cards.title: Incentive spirometer goal
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prevents atelectasis by improving lung expansion.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: quick shallow breaths don’t help—slow deep inspiration matters.

cards.title: Atelectasis early sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Diminished breath sounds and low-grade fever post-op.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: waiting for high fever delays prevention actions.

cards.title: Aspiration risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: High risk with decreased LOC, dysphagia, tube feeds.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: supine feeding increases aspiration.

cards.title: Aspiration first action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Turn on side, suction airway, apply O2.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: giving water ‘to clear throat’ worsens aspiration.

cards.title: DVT classic clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Unilateral swelling, warmth, pain.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t massage the leg—embolization risk.

cards.title: PE red flags
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, tachycardia.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: normal lung sounds can still occur with PE.

cards.title: Suspected PE priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Apply O2, elevate HOB, rapid assessment, notify provider/activate protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: sending patient to walk to CT without stability is unsafe.

cards.title: Anticoag teaching baseline
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Bleeding precautions and consistent follow-up.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: NSAIDs increase bleeding risk.

cards.title: HF fluid overload signs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Crackles, edema, weight gain, JVD.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘clear lungs’ doesn’t exclude HF if right-sided signs dominate.

cards.title: HF daily weights
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Same time, same scale, same clothing.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: waiting for edema misses early fluid gain.

cards.title: HF first-line nursing action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Position upright and give O2 if dyspneic.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: starting a new IV before fixing breathing delays care.

cards.title: Pulmonary edema frothy sputum
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pink frothy sputum suggests acute pulmonary edema.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treat as emergency—don’t just ‘reassess later’.

cards.title: Loop diuretic timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Give earlier in day when possible to reduce nocturia.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: holding diuretic because ‘BP is okay’ ignores fluid overload.

cards.title: ACE/ARB in HF
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Reduces remodeling and afterload.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: monitor K+ and renal function—don’t ignore labs.

cards.title: MI atypical in women/elderly
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: May present with nausea, fatigue, SOB, jaw/back pain.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: no chest pain ≠ no MI.

cards.title: Chest pain priority bundle
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Get ECG, assess vitals, apply O2 if hypoxic, IV access per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: waiting for troponin before acting delays care.

cards.title: Aspirin in ACS
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Chewable aspirin reduces platelet aggregation (unless contraindicated).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: enteric-coated isn’t preferred for acute onset.

cards.title: Nitro: when to hold
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hold if hypotension or recent PDE5 inhibitor use.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: giving nitro to a low BP patient can cause collapse.

cards.title: Morphine caution
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Used for pain if unrelieved, but monitor respiratory status and BP.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t mask worsening symptoms without reassessment.

cards.title: Sinus rhythm criteria
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Regular rate, P before each QRS, consistent PR.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: artifact can mimic arrhythmia—check patient first.

cards.title: AFib key feature
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Irregularly irregular rhythm, no distinct P waves.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: rate control doesn’t remove clot risk—anticoag may be needed.

cards.title: VTach unstable signs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hypotension, chest pain, altered LOC = unstable.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treat the patient, not just the monitor.

cards.title: Vfib action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Start CPR and defibrillate ASAP per ACLS.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: searching for pulse too long delays shock.

cards.title: Asystole action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: CPR + epi; NOT shockable.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: defibrillation doesn’t fix asystole.

cards.title: PAC/PVC basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Ectopic beats can be triggered by hypoxia/electrolytes.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treat causes (O2, K/Mg) before antiarrhythmics.

cards.title: Bradycardia nursing check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess symptoms and perfusion (BP, mentation).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: a low HR can be normal in athletes—symptoms guide urgency.

cards.title: Tachycardia cause hunt
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pain, fever, hypovolemia, hypoxia are common causes.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: giving beta-blocker before fixing hypoxia can worsen outcome.

cards.title: BiPAP/CPAP contraindication
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Requires alert patient who can protect airway.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: vomiting/low LOC = aspiration risk—don’t force mask.

cards.title: Vent alarm priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Look at the patient first, then troubleshoot equipment.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: silencing alarm without assessment is unsafe.

cards.title: High-pressure alarm causes
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Kink, biting tube, secretions, bronchospasm.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: disconnecting from vent removes PEEP and can worsen oxygenation.

cards.title: Low-pressure alarm causes
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Disconnection, leak, cuff issue.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t ignore—patient can lose ventilation fast.

cards.title: Trach: accidental decannulation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Maintain airway; use spare trach/obturator per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: leaving stoma open without action can lead to airway loss.

cards.title: Trach suctioning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sterile technique and pre-oxygenate.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: suctioning too long causes hypoxia/bradycardia.

cards.title: Chest tube purpose
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Removes air/blood to restore negative pressure.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: clamping can cause tension pneumothorax unless ordered.

cards.title: Water-seal bubbling
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Intermittent bubbling may be normal early with air leak resolution.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: continuous bubbling can mean leak—check connections.

cards.title: Tidaling meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Fluid level rises/falls with breathing—often expected.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: no tidaling may mean obstruction or lung re-expansion—assess.

cards.title: Chest tube disconnection
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Place tube end in sterile water to re-establish seal, then call provider.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: clamping a disconnected tube can trap air.

cards.title: Chest tube pulled out
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Apply occlusive dressing (3-sided if pneumothorax risk) and notify.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: leaving open to air can worsen collapse.

cards.title: Pneumothorax sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sudden SOB, unilateral decreased sounds.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: giving more pain meds doesn’t fix ventilation.

cards.title: Tension pneumothorax clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tracheal deviation, hypotension, severe distress = emergency.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: wait for x-ray can be fatal—decompress per protocol.

cards.title: O2 fire safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Oxygen supports combustion—keep away from flames/oils.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: petroleum-based lotion increases fire risk near O2.

cards.title: Smoking with O2
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: No smoking near oxygen equipment.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘turning off O2 for a minute’ is still dangerous with residual O2.

cards.title: Diuretics and K+
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Loop/thiazide can lower K+ → dysrhythmia risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: muscle weakness/cramps are warning signs.

cards.title: Beta-blocker patient education
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Don’t stop abruptly; monitor HR/BP.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: sudden stop can cause rebound tachycardia/angina.

cards.title: Shock early sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tachycardia and cool skin can appear before hypotension.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘normal BP’ doesn’t rule out shock early.

cards.title: Septic shock clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Warm skin early, fever, tachycardia; later cool/clammy.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: waiting for positive cultures delays antibiotics per protocol.

cards.title: Fluid resuscitation priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Large-bore IV and isotonic fluids per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: diuretics are not used in hypovolemic shock.

cards.title: Transfusion reaction first action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: STOP transfusion, keep IV open with NS, assess.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘slow the rate’ is wrong for reaction.

cards.title: TRALI vs TACO clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: TRALI = acute lung injury; TACO = fluid overload.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: both cause SOB—look at BP/JVD/response to diuretics.

cards.title: COPD vs asthma breath sounds
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: COPD often has diminished sounds; asthma often wheeze.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘no wheeze’ can still be severe asthma (silent chest).

cards.title: Barrel chest mechanism
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Air trapping increases AP diameter.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: not an acute sign of pneumothorax.

cards.title: Pneumonia positioning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Turn, cough, deep breathe; position for drainage if appropriate.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: bedrest alone increases atelectasis.

cards.title: O2 toxicity
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prolonged high FiO2 can damage lungs.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: use lowest FiO2 to maintain target SpO2 per orders.

cards.title: Sputum color meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Change in color/amount can suggest infection.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: clear sputum doesn’t exclude pneumonia in elderly.

cards.title: COPD nutrition
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Small frequent meals reduce dyspnea while eating.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: large meals increase diaphragmatic pressure.

cards.title: Orthopnea clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Needing pillows suggests HF/pulmonary congestion.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: lying flat worsens venous return to lungs.

cards.title: HF med compliance teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Daily weights and low-sodium diet reduce exacerbations.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘skip diuretic on travel days’ leads to overload.

cards.title: STEMI time sensitivity
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Time is myocardium—activate rapid protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘wait and see’ with persistent symptoms loses heart muscle.

cards.title: Troponin timing trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Troponin may be negative early.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t rule out MI from a single early troponin.

cards.title: O2 in MI
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Give O2 only if hypoxic per many protocols.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: routine O2 for everyone is outdated—follow facility policy.

cards.title: Pain assessment in ACS
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Reassess after nitro/meds and monitor BP.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: repeated nitro without BP checks is unsafe.

cards.title: AFib anticoag rationale
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Irregular atrial contraction → clot risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: converting rhythm doesn’t erase stroke risk immediately.

cards.title: PVCs and electrolytes
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Low K/Mg increases PVCs.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treating PVCs with antiarrhythmic first misses cause.

cards.title: Chest tube output monitoring
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Mark drainage, report sudden large increases.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: tipping chamber breaks measurement accuracy.

cards.title: Pleural effusion vs pneumothorax
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Effusion = dullness; pneumothorax = hyperresonance/decreased sounds.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: both cause SOB—assessment guides.

cards.title: Thoracentesis positioning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sit upright leaning forward if tolerated.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: lying flat increases dyspnea.

cards.title: Thoracentesis complication
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Monitor for pneumothorax after procedure.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: sudden SOB post-procedure is not ‘expected’.

cards.title: Inhaler order
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Bronchodilator before steroid opens airways.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: steroid first reduces delivery depth.

cards.title: Spacer benefit
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Spacer improves med delivery to lungs.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: spraying into mouth without inhale wastes dose.

cards.title: Nebulizer teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Slow deep breaths improve deposition.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: rapid shallow breathing reduces medication delivery.

cards.title: V/Q mismatch concept
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: O2 helps hypoxemia; ventilation issues may need airway support.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: O2 doesn’t fix mucus plugging—need suction/bronchodilator.

cards.title: Stridor meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stridor is upper airway obstruction.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treat as emergency; not the same as wheeze.

cards.title: Epiglottitis caution
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Do not force throat exam if suspected.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: agitation can worsen obstruction—keep calm and prepare airway.

cards.title: Croup vs asthma sound
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Croup = barking cough/stridor.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: albuterol helps wheeze, not stridor.

cards.title: Pulmonary embolism anticoag rationale
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prevents clot extension and new clots.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: anticoag doesn’t ‘dissolve’ clot immediately.

cards.title: Aortic dissection clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tearing pain, unequal BP arms.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: thrombolytics are dangerous if dissection suspected.

cards.title: Pericarditis pain
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Worse supine, better leaning forward.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treat like ACS until ruled out if uncertain.

cards.title: Cardiac tamponade triad
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Beck’s triad: hypotension, JVD, muffled sounds.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: fluid bolus may help temporarily; needs urgent intervention.

cards.title: Priority check #102
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: When symptoms worsen, reassess vitals, breath sounds, and mental status.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: documenting without reassessment misses deterioration.

cards.title: Priority check #103
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: When symptoms worsen, reassess vitals, breath sounds, and mental status.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: documenting without reassessment misses deterioration.

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: When symptoms worsen, reassess vitals, breath sounds, and mental status.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: documenting without reassessment misses deterioration.

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: When symptoms worsen, reassess vitals, breath sounds, and mental status.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: documenting without reassessment misses deterioration.

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: When symptoms worsen, reassess vitals, breath sounds, and mental status.

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: When symptoms worsen, reassess vitals, breath sounds, and mental status.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: documenting without reassessment misses deterioration.

modules.title: 6. Adult Health (Med-Surg) I: Cardio-Resp

modules.moduleDescription: High-yield adult med-surg covering neuro emergencies (stroke, seizures, ICP), renal/urinary issues (AKI, dialysis, UTI), endocrine crises (DKA/HHS, thyroid), and GI/hepatic problems (bleed, pancreatitis, cirrhosis) with NCLEX priorities and traps.

cards.title: Stroke: time is brain
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Activate stroke protocol immediately for sudden neuro deficits.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t give food/water—swallow screen first.

cards.title: Stroke first nursing action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess airway, glucose, and onset time; then rapid transport/CT per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treating low glucose can reverse ‘stroke-like’ signs—check it early.

cards.title: Ischemic vs hemorrhagic stroke
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: CT is needed before thrombolytics.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: giving aspirin or tPA before CT can worsen hemorrhage.

cards.title: tPA contraindication cue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Bleeding risk and time window determine eligibility.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: uncontrolled BP or recent surgery can exclude tPA.

cards.title: Post-stroke aspiration risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Dysphagia is common after stroke.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: thick liquids may be safer, but only after evaluation.

cards.title: Unilateral neglect
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Right hemispheric stroke can cause neglect of left side.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: patient may deny deficit—use cues and safety measures.

cards.title: Increased ICP triad
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cushing’s triad: HTN, bradycardia, irregular respirations.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: this is late—act before it appears.

cards.title: ICP positioning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Elevate HOB ~30° and keep neck midline.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: hip flexion/Trendelenburg increases ICP.

cards.title: ICP: avoid Valsalva
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prevent coughing/straining that raises ICP.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: no vigorous suctioning without pre-oxygenation and limit time.

cards.title: Seizure precautions basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protect from injury; pad rails; oxygen/suction ready.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t restrain limbs or put objects in mouth.

cards.title: Active seizure priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Turn to side, protect head, time seizure.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: trying to force oral meds during seizure is unsafe.

cards.title: Postictal phase
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Confusion and fatigue after seizure are expected.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: sudden ‘not waking up’ can also signal status epilepticus—assess.

cards.title: Status epilepticus
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Continuous seizures = emergency.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: airway/breathing and IV benzos are priority per protocol.

cards.title: Meningitis isolation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Droplet precautions until treated per policy.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: fever + stiff neck is emergency—don’t delay antibiotics/lumbar eval.

cards.title: Spinal cord injury: neurogenic shock
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hypotension with bradycardia after SCI suggests neurogenic shock.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: not all shock has tachycardia.

cards.title: Autonomic dysreflexia trigger
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: T6+ SCI: noxious stimulus (full bladder/bowel) causes severe HTN.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: sit up and remove stimulus—this is emergent.

cards.title: Autonomic dysreflexia first action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sit patient upright and check bladder catheter/kinks.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: giving antihypertensive without removing trigger may fail.

cards.title: Lumbar puncture aftercare
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Monitor for headache; lie flat per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: new neuro changes post-LP need urgent evaluation.

cards.title: Head injury: clear fluid check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: CSF leak from nose/ear suggests basilar skull fracture.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: do not pack nose; report and maintain sterile dressing.

cards.title: Basilar skull fracture sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Battle sign or raccoon eyes indicates serious injury.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: NG tube may be contraindicated—check provider order.

cards.title: DKA hallmark
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: DKA = hyperglycemia + ketosis + acidosis.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: Kussmaul respirations are compensation—don’t suppress.

cards.title: DKA first priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Start fluids and insulin per protocol; monitor K+ closely.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: insulin drives K+ into cells—can cause hypokalemia.

cards.title: DKA potassium paradox
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Serum K+ may be high, but total body K+ is low.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: after insulin, K+ can drop fast—replace as ordered.

cards.title: HHS vs DKA
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: HHS has very high glucose and dehydration, minimal ketosis.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: neuro changes can be prominent—watch LOC.

cards.title: Hypoglycemia vs DKA symptoms
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hypoglycemia = sweaty/shaky/confused; DKA = thirsty, polyuria, fruity breath.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: beta-blockers can mask hypoglycemia signs.

cards.title: Thyroid storm
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hyperthyroid crisis: fever, tachycardia, agitation.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treat as emergency—cooling + meds per protocol.

cards.title: Myxedema coma
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Severe hypothyroid: hypothermia, bradycardia, hypotension.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: sedatives/opioids can worsen hypoventilation—use caution.

cards.title: Adrenal crisis clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Low BP, weakness, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: needs steroids and fluids—don’t delay.

cards.title: Steroid sick-day rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stress/illness may require increased steroid dose per plan.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: stopping steroids abruptly can trigger crisis.

cards.title: Diabetes foot care
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Inspect daily; no barefoot; trim nails carefully.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: heating pads can burn neuropathic feet.

cards.title: Diabetes: infection masking
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hyperglycemia impairs immunity; infections may present subtly.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘no fever’ doesn’t rule out infection in diabetics.

cards.title: AKI early sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rising creatinine can precede oliguria.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: urine output can be misleading in early AKI.

cards.title: Prerenal AKI cause
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Dehydration/low perfusion causes prerenal AKI.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: NSAIDs can worsen renal perfusion.

cards.title: Hyperkalemia red flag
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tall peaked T waves, weakness, dysrhythmias.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: life-threatening—treat before ‘rechecking later’.

cards.title: Hyperkalemia immediate actions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cardiac monitoring, calcium, insulin/glucose, albuterol per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: kayexalate works slowly—don’t rely on it acutely.

cards.title: Dialysis fistula care
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: No BP/IV/venipuncture in fistula arm.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: palpate thrill and auscultate bruit each shift.

cards.title: Dialysis disequilibrium
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rapid fluid shifts can cause headache, nausea, confusion.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: new neuro symptoms during dialysis need urgent assessment.

cards.title: Peritoneal dialysis outflow
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cloudy outflow suggests peritonitis.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: report immediately—don’t discard sample.

cards.title: UTI in elderly
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Confusion and falls may be presenting signs.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: absence of dysuria doesn’t rule out UTI.

cards.title: Pyelonephritis warning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Fever + flank pain suggests upper UTI.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: untreated can progress to sepsis.

cards.title: Kidney stone priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pain control + strain urine; monitor for obstruction.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: no fluids if contraindicated, but dehydration worsens stones.

cards.title: Post-op urinary retention
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Scan bladder if no void; assess distention.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: forcing fluids doesn’t fix retention.

cards.title: Nephrotic syndrome clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Proteinuria, edema, frothy urine.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: infection and clot risk increase—monitor.

cards.title: GI bleed priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess hemodynamics: vitals, mental status, perfusion.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: focusing on nausea before stabilizing circulation is unsafe.

cards.title: Upper GI bleed sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Coffee-ground emesis or melena suggests upper bleed.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: iron supplements can darken stool—assess for other signs.

cards.title: Variceal bleed risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cirrhosis can cause esophageal varices—massive bleed risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: avoid NG insertion without provider direction.

cards.title: Lactulose purpose
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Lactulose lowers ammonia in hepatic encephalopathy.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: goal is 2–3 soft stools/day; stopping for diarrhea can worsen ammonia.

cards.title: Hepatic encephalopathy clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Confusion, asterixis, high ammonia.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: sedatives can worsen mental status—use cautiously.

cards.title: Ascites care basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Low-sodium diet, diuretics, monitor weight/abdominal girth.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: sudden resp distress can occur if fluid shifts—watch.

cards.title: Pancreatitis hallmark
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Severe epigastric pain radiating to back + elevated lipase.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: keep NPO and manage pain/fluids—food worsens stimulation.

cards.title: Pancreatitis calcium trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hypocalcemia can occur (fat saponification).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: tingling/tetany needs assessment.

cards.title: Bowel obstruction sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: High-pitched sounds early, absent late; distention, vomiting.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: laxatives can perforate obstruction.

cards.title: NG tube for obstruction
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Decompresses stomach and reduces vomiting/aspiration risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: low intermittent suction is common—don’t clamp without order.

cards.title: Appendicitis rebound pain
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sudden relief of pain can mean rupture.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t apply heat—risk of rupture increases.

cards.title: Diverticulitis teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Acute: bowel rest/low fiber; after: high fiber.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: seeds/nuts restriction is no longer universal—follow provider plan.

cards.title: C. diff isolation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Contact precautions; soap and water hand hygiene.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: alcohol gel doesn’t kill spores effectively.

cards.title: IBD vs IBS clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: IBD has inflammation and bleeding; IBS doesn’t.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: weight loss and anemia suggest IBD, not IBS.

cards.title: Ostomy output check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Ileostomy output is more liquid; watch dehydration.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: no output + cramps can mean obstruction.

cards.title: Neuro checks trend
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Trend is more important than single number.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: small changes in LOC can signal worsening ICP.

cards.title: Pupil changes urgency
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Unequal pupils can indicate herniation.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘sleepy’ after head injury is not always normal.

cards.title: Stroke positioning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: HOB elevated; support affected side; prevent shoulder subluxation.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: pulling arm during transfers can injure shoulder.

cards.title: Thrombolytic bleeding watch
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: After tPA, monitor for bleeding and neuro changes.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: avoid unnecessary sticks/IM injections post-tPA.

cards.title: Hyponatremia neuro risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Severe hyponatremia can cause seizures.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: correcting too fast can cause osmotic demyelination.

cards.title: Hypernatremia clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Thirst, dry mucosa, neuro irritability.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: rapid free-water correction can cause cerebral edema.

cards.title: Fluid overload vs deficit
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Overload: edema/JVD/crackles; deficit: tachycardia/dry mucosa/orthostasis.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: BP can be normal early in both—look at trends.

cards.title: Orthostatic hypotension
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Drop in BP on standing suggests volume depletion.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: encourage slow position changes to prevent falls.

cards.title: Insulin onset timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Match rapid-acting insulin to food intake.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: giving without meal available → hypoglycemia.

cards.title: Metformin contrast hold
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hold metformin around IV contrast per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: lactic acidosis risk rises if kidneys injured.

cards.title: Levothyroxine teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Take on empty stomach, separate from iron/calcium.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: symptoms improve slowly—don’t self-adjust dose.

cards.title: Seizure aura clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some patients have warning sensations.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: aura is not a ‘panic attack’—prepare safety.

cards.title: Todd’s paralysis
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Temporary weakness after seizure can mimic stroke.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: assess timeline; still evaluate urgently if unsure.

cards.title: ICP: temperature control
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Fever increases metabolic demand and ICP.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘mild fever’ in neuro patient can worsen outcomes.

cards.title: Diabetes: sick day ketones
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Check ketones when ill or glucose high.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: vomiting + high sugars can be DKA even without huge numbers.

cards.title: Dialysis weight rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Dry weight guides fluid removal.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: comparing to yesterday’s weight without dry weight misleads.

cards.title: Renal diet basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Often restrict Na, K, and phosphorus in CKD.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: salt substitutes may contain potassium.

cards.title: Hyperphosphatemia binder
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Phosphate binders taken with meals.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: taking between meals reduces effectiveness.

cards.title: GI bleed meds caution
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid NSAIDs in GI bleed risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘it helps pain’ can worsen bleeding.

cards.title: Liver disease bleeding
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cirrhosis reduces clotting factors.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: normal platelets don’t guarantee normal coagulation.

cards.title: Ammonia and protein
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protein restriction depends on plan; avoid drastic changes without orders.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘no protein ever’ is not standard for all cirrhosis.

cards.title: Pancreatitis alcohol role
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Alcohol and gallstones are common causes.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: restarting alcohol increases recurrence risk.

cards.title: Cholecystitis after fatty meal
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: RUQ pain after fatty foods suggests gallbladder issue.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: Murphy’s sign suggests inflammation—needs evaluation.

cards.title: Post-op ileus
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: No bowel sounds and distention after surgery can be ileus.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: giving laxatives can worsen symptoms.

cards.title: GI perforation signs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rigid abdomen, severe pain, rebound tenderness.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treat as emergency—don’t give oral meds/food.

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If a patient’s condition changes, reassess ABCs and trend neuro/renal status.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: relying on one normal value can miss rapid deterioration.
