modules.title: 7. Adult Health (Med-Surg) II: Neuro • Renal • Endocrine • GI

modules.moduleDescription: NCLEX mental health essentials: therapeutic communication, safety (suicide/violence), anxiety/depression, psychosis, substance use, mood disorders, key meds and crisis priorities, with high-yield traps and boundary rules.

cards.title: Therapeutic vs nontherapeutic
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use open-ended, feelings-focused responses.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: avoid ‘why’ questions—they can sound blaming.

cards.title: Silence as a tool
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Silence allows processing and encourages sharing.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: filling silence with advice shuts patients down.

cards.title: Reflection
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Repeat key feelings/words to clarify.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: parroting without emotion sounds robotic—reflect meaning.

cards.title: Restating
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Restate content to confirm understanding.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t add your own assumptions.

cards.title: Exploring
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Ask for more detail about feelings/meaning.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘Tell me more’ is better than rapid-fire questions.

cards.title: Focusing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Direct conversation to one topic at a time.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: jumping topics increases anxiety.

cards.title: Giving information
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Provide facts to reduce uncertainty.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: giving advice (‘you should…’) removes patient autonomy.

cards.title: Advice trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid telling patients what to do.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: instead offer options and support decision-making.

cards.title: False reassurance
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid “Everything will be fine.”
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: use “I’m here with you” or “Let’s talk about what worries you.”

cards.title: Changing the subject
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Do not abruptly change topics.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: it signals you can’t handle their feelings.

cards.title: Closed questions use
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Closed questions are for specific facts, not emotional exploration.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: overuse can feel like interrogation.

cards.title: Summarizing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Summarize to end or transition sessions.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: include the patient’s words; don’t reinterpret.

cards.title: Suicide priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Safety is first: assess plan, means, intent.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: asking about suicide does NOT ‘plant the idea’.

cards.title: Suicide high-risk cue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Plan + means + time frame + prior attempt = high risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘cheerful mood’ can occur after deciding to act.

cards.title: One-to-one observation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Continuous observation requires constant visual monitoring.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘checks every 15 min’ ≠ 1:1.

cards.title: Means restriction
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Remove belts, sharps, cords; safe environment.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: bathroom access may need supervision.

cards.title: Contracts for safety trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: No-harm contracts are not reliable alone.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: use observation and environmental controls.

cards.title: Violence escalation signs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pacing, clenched fists, loud voice, staring.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: address early; don’t wait until assault happens.

cards.title: De-escalation basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Calm voice, space, simple choices, set limits.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: multiple staff talking at once escalates.

cards.title: Limit setting
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Set clear, consistent limits with consequences.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t threaten punishments you can’t enforce.

cards.title: Restraint last resort
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use least restrictive measures; follow policy orders and monitoring.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: restraints are not for staff convenience.

cards.title: Restraint monitoring
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess circulation, airway, skin, toileting/hydration per policy.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: leaving restrained patient unattended is unsafe.

cards.title: Panic attack priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stay with patient; reduce stimuli; coach slow breathing.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: telling them ‘calm down’ increases distress.

cards.title: Anxiety levels clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Mild improves learning; moderate narrows focus; severe/panic impairs.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: teaching during panic won’t stick.

cards.title: Grounding technique
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Orient to reality (name 5 things you see, etc.).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: debating their fear isn’t effective in panic.

cards.title: Depression assessment
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess sleep, appetite, energy, and suicidal thoughts.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘I’m fine’ doesn’t equal safe—ask directly.

cards.title: Antidepressant onset
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SSRIs take weeks for full effect.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: early energy increase can raise suicide risk—monitor.

cards.title: SSRI side effects basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: GI upset, sexual dysfunction, insomnia or somnolence.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t stop abruptly—withdrawal symptoms.

cards.title: Mania nursing priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protect from injury; reduce stimuli; set limits.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: long discussions increase agitation.

cards.title: Mania communication
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use short, direct statements and firm limits.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: arguing about delusions escalates.

cards.title: Mania nutrition
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Provide high-calorie finger foods and fluids.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: patient may not sit for meals—plan accordingly.

cards.title: Sleep in mania
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Promote rest with quiet environment and routine.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: caffeine worsens mania/anxiety.

cards.title: Hallucination response
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Acknowledge feelings and present reality.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t say ‘Yes, I hear it too’ (validates hallucination).

cards.title: Command hallucinations
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess if voices command harm to self/others.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: command hallucinations increase immediate risk.

cards.title: Delusion response
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Do not argue; focus on feelings and reality-based topics.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: trying to ‘prove’ them wrong increases mistrust.

cards.title: Paranoia approach
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use clear explanations; avoid whispering and sudden touch.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: too many staff can feel threatening.

cards.title: Alcohol withdrawal timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Can begin hours after last drink; severe cases progress quickly.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: early tremors can precede seizures/DTs.

cards.title: Delirium tremens clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Severe agitation, hallucinations, fever, HTN, tachycardia.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: DTs are medical emergency—monitor closely.

cards.title: Benzodiazepines in withdrawal
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Benzos are common first-line for alcohol withdrawal.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: giving stimulants/coffee doesn’t treat withdrawal.

cards.title: Opioid withdrawal
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Flu-like symptoms, yawning, cramps, diarrhea.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: distressing but usually not life-threatening like DTs.

cards.title: Naloxone and relapse risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: After naloxone, monitor for re-sedation and withdrawal agitation.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: one naloxone dose may wear off before opioid.

cards.title: Stimulant intoxication
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cocaine/meth: agitation, HTN, chest pain.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: beta-blockers can be risky—follow protocol.

cards.title: Anorexia priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Medical stability: vitals, electrolytes, weight trends.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: bradycardia/hypothermia can be life-threatening.

cards.title: Bulimia complication
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Electrolyte disturbances (low K+) → dysrhythmias.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: normal BMI doesn’t exclude bulimia.

cards.title: Meal supervision
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Supervise after meals to prevent purging when indicated.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: bathroom breaks immediately after meals can be risky.

cards.title: PTSD triggers
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Triggers can cause flashbacks and hyperarousal.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: forcing detailed recounting early can retraumatize.

cards.title: Trauma-informed care
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Offer choice, explain actions, ask permission.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: sudden touch can trigger panic.

cards.title: Lithium hydration
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Maintain consistent fluids and sodium.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: dehydration raises lithium → toxicity.

cards.title: Lithium toxicity sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tremor, GI upset, confusion, ataxia.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: NSAIDs/diuretics can increase lithium levels.

cards.title: Antipsychotic EPS
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treat dystonia urgently (airway risk if laryngeal).

cards.title: Tardive dyskinesia
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Late, potentially irreversible involuntary movements.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: report early; don’t dismiss as ‘nervous habit’.

cards.title: NMS red flags
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Fever, rigidity, altered mental status, autonomic instability.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: stop antipsychotic and get urgent care—don’t give more.

cards.title: Clozapine agranulocytosis
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Monitor ANC; report fever/sore throat.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: infection signs require immediate action.

cards.title: Benzodiazepine caution
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Risk of sedation/falls and dependence.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: mix with alcohol/opioids increases respiratory depression.

cards.title: MAOI food rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid tyramine foods to prevent hypertensive crisis.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘one cheat meal’ can be dangerous.

cards.title: Serotonin syndrome
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Agitation, hyperreflexia, diaphoresis, diarrhea.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: combining SSRIs with certain meds (e.g., MAOIs) raises risk.

cards.title: Milieu therapy basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Structured environment supports behavior change.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: inconsistent rules increase manipulation/conflict.

cards.title: Group therapy boundary
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Share respectfully; maintain confidentiality.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: giving graphic details can trigger others.

cards.title: Confidentiality rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Share only with care team on need-to-know basis.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: family requests require patient consent unless exceptions apply.

cards.title: Informed consent
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Patient must understand risks/benefits and choose voluntarily.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: sedation/confusion invalidates consent—notify provider.

cards.title: Least restrictive environment
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use minimum restriction needed for safety.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: seclusion/restraints require documentation and monitoring.

cards.title: Best response format
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pick answer that is therapeutic, safe, and patient-centered.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: avoid ‘why’ and avoid advising/arguing.

cards.title: First vs best action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ‘First’ is immediate safety/assessment; ‘best’ is overall plan.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t jump to teaching before stabilizing.

cards.title: Setting limits with manipulative behavior
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Be consistent and matter-of-fact.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: negotiating repeatedly reinforces manipulation.

cards.title: Splitting behavior
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Staff should communicate consistently to prevent splitting.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: taking sides increases conflict.

cards.title: Therapeutic touch caution
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Touch can comfort but may be misinterpreted.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: always ask permission and consider trauma history.

cards.title: Grief vs depression
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Grief can include sadness but preserves self-worth; depression often includes hopelessness.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: suicidal ideation is not ‘normal grief’—assess.

cards.title: Crisis intervention goal
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Focus on immediate problem and safety in short term.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: deep childhood analysis isn’t crisis work.

cards.title: Obsessions vs compulsions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Obsessions = intrusive thoughts; compulsions = repetitive acts.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: forbidding rituals abruptly can raise anxiety.

cards.title: OCD nursing approach
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Allow time-limited rituals initially, then gradual reduction.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: confrontation increases anxiety and resistance.

cards.title: Phobia exposure
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Gradual exposure and coping skills help reduce phobia response.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: forced exposure can traumatize.

cards.title: Somatic symptom focus
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Acknowledge symptoms, shift to coping and function.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: saying ‘it’s all in your head’ is nontherapeutic.

cards.title: Conversion disorder
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Neuro symptoms without organic cause; symptoms are real to patient.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: implying faking increases distress.

cards.title: Personality disorder boundaries
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Clear boundaries and consistent rules are key.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: over-involvement leads to boundary violations.

cards.title: Borderline splitting risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Fear of abandonment drives behavior.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: inconsistent staff responses worsen splitting.

cards.title: ADHD stimulant timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Give stimulants early day to reduce insomnia.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: late doses worsen sleep and appetite suppression.

cards.title: Child abuse reporting
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Nurses are mandated reporters when abuse is suspected.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t investigate—report per policy/law.

cards.title: Intimate partner violence screening
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use private setting and direct, nonjudgmental questions.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: asking in front of partner is unsafe.

cards.title: Elder abuse clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Inconsistent stories, poor hygiene, unexplained injuries.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: patient may fear retaliation—ensure safety.

cards.title: Sleep hygiene basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Routine, limit screens/caffeine, quiet environment.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: alcohol may worsen sleep quality.

cards.title: Depression nutrition
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Small goals and protein/calorie support may help energy.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: telling patient to ‘just eat’ is not supportive.

cards.title: Anxiety teaching timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Teach coping when anxiety is mild/moderate, not panic.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: education during panic is ineffective.

cards.title: Psychosis safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Reduce stimuli and provide simple, clear choices.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: joking can be misinterpreted as threatening.

cards.title: Paranoid patient meds
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Explain each medication clearly before giving.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: unexpected meds increase refusal and suspicion.

cards.title: Withdrawal seizures risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Alcohol withdrawal can cause seizures.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: seizure precautions and meds are priority.

cards.title: CAGE screening cue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: CAGE questions screen for alcohol misuse.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: screening is not diagnosis—follow with assessment.

cards.title: SMART goals in therapy
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Goals should be specific and achievable.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: vague goals (‘be happier’) are hard to measure.

cards.title: Therapeutic boundaries
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid dual relationships and personal disclosures.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: giving your phone number is a boundary violation.

cards.title: Active listening
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use minimal encouragers (nods, ‘mm-hmm’).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: interrupting to ‘fix’ stops disclosure.

Takeaway/Trap: Trap: advice, arguing, and false reassurance are common wrong answers.

modules.title: 8. Mental Health

modules.moduleDescription: NCLEX OB essentials: pregnancy assessment, labor stages, fetal monitoring basics, postpartum complications, newborn care, and emergency priorities (preeclampsia, hemorrhage), with high-yield traps and safety actions.

cards.title: Pregnancy danger signs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Bleeding, severe headache, vision changes, RUQ pain, decreased fetal movement are red flags.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: mild nausea is common; severe symptoms need urgent eval.

cards.title: Fetal movement teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Count kicks; report decreased movement.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: waiting ‘until tomorrow’ can delay care.

cards.title: Supine hypotension
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pregnant patient supine can compress vena cava.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: turn to left side to improve BP and perfusion.

cards.title: Rh incompatibility basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rh- mother may need Rho(D) immune globulin.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: give at 28 weeks and after birth/procedures if baby Rh+ (per protocol).

cards.title: RhoGAM not a vaccine
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: RhoGAM prevents antibody formation, not treats it.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: it doesn’t help if mother already sensitized.

cards.title: Gestational diabetes screening
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Often screened mid-pregnancy per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: diet teaching matters even if ‘no symptoms’.

cards.title: GBS prophylaxis
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: GBS+ mothers often get intrapartum antibiotics.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: antibiotics are during labor, not weeks before.

cards.title: Preeclampsia hallmark
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: HTN after 20 weeks + proteinuria or end-organ signs.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: edema alone is not diagnostic.

cards.title: Severe preeclampsia signs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Severe BP, headache, vision changes, RUQ pain, low platelets.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: RUQ pain can signal liver involvement—urgent.

cards.title: Eclampsia prevention
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Magnesium sulfate helps prevent seizures.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: Mg is not primarily an antihypertensive.

cards.title: Magnesium toxicity
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Loss of DTRs, respiratory depression, decreased LOC.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: keep calcium gluconate available as antidote.

cards.title: Mg monitoring priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess RR, reflexes, urine output.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: normal BP doesn’t mean Mg is safe.

cards.title: Eclamptic seizure action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protect airway, turn to side, give O2; continue Mg per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t restrain; prevent aspiration.

cards.title: Preeclampsia BP meds
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Antihypertensives lower stroke risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: lowering BP doesn’t remove seizure risk—Mg still needed.

cards.title: Labor stages
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stage 1: dilation; Stage 2: pushing/birth; Stage 3: placenta; Stage 4: recovery.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: transition is late Stage 1 (8–10 cm).

cards.title: True vs false labor
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: True labor contractions get regular/stronger and change cervix.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: Braxton Hicks don’t cause cervical change.

cards.title: Rupture of membranes priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess fetal HR first after ROM.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: cord prolapse can occur—FHR check is immediate.

cards.title: Cord prolapse action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Knee-chest, relieve pressure with gloved hand, call for help.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: do not attempt to push cord back in.

cards.title: Amniotic fluid odor/color
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Foul odor suggests infection; green suggests meconium.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: pink-tinged can be normal ‘bloody show’.

cards.title: Meconium aspiration risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Meconium can signal fetal stress.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: prepare neonatal support; not always emergency but needs readiness.

cards.title: Pain control epidural
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess BP and FHR; monitor for hypotension.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: hypotension can reduce placental perfusion—treat promptly.

cards.title: Oxytocin safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Titrate per protocol; monitor contractions and FHR.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: tachysystole (too many contractions) requires stopping/adjusting.

cards.title: Uterine tachysystole
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Too frequent contractions reduce fetal oxygenation.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: first action is usually stop oxytocin, reposition, O2 per protocol.

cards.title: Early decelerations
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Mirror contractions; usually head compression.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: generally benign—don’t panic.

cards.title: Variable decelerations
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Abrupt drops; cord compression.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: reposition mother first; consider amnioinfusion per order.

cards.title: Late decelerations
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Begin after contraction peak; uteroplacental insufficiency.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: intrauterine resuscitation (left side, stop oxytocin, O2, fluids) + notify.

cards.title: Accelerations
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Reassuring sign of fetal well-being.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: absence of accelerations isn’t always bad but needs context.

cards.title: Baseline variability
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Moderate variability is reassuring.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: minimal variability can be sleep, meds, or hypoxia—assess trends.

cards.title: Uterine atony cause
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Boggy uterus is most common cause of postpartum hemorrhage.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: first action: fundal massage and assess lochia.

cards.title: Postpartum fundus check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Fundus should be firm and midline.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: deviated fundus often means full bladder—assist to void.

cards.title: Lochia progression
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rubra → serosa → alba over time.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: large clots/heavy bleeding is not normal.

cards.title: Hemorrhage priority actions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Massage fundus, call for help, meds per protocol, IV fluids.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t leave patient alone while bleeding heavily.

cards.title: Uterotonic meds caution
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some uterotonics contraindicated in HTN/asthma.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: check med specifics before giving.

cards.title: Postpartum infection sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Fever, uterine tenderness, foul lochia.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: mild chills after birth can be normal; persistent fever is not.

cards.title: Postpartum preeclampsia
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Preeclampsia can occur after delivery.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: new headache/vision changes postpartum need urgent evaluation.

cards.title: DVT postpartum risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hypercoagulable state raises DVT risk postpartum.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: encourage early ambulation unless contraindicated.

cards.title: Postpartum depression clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Persistent sadness, anhedonia, bonding issues beyond 2 weeks.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘baby blues’ are brief; suicidal thoughts require emergency care.

cards.title: Newborn airway priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Warm, dry, stimulate; clear airway if needed.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: cold stress worsens hypoglycemia and respiratory distress.

cards.title: Newborn temperature control
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Newborns lose heat quickly.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t bathe until temperature stable.

cards.title: APGAR timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Scored at 1 and 5 minutes.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: APGAR doesn’t predict long-term outcomes; it guides immediate status.

cards.title: Vitamin K purpose
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prevents hemorrhagic disease of newborn.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: it’s not a vaccine; it supports clotting factors.

cards.title: Erythromycin eye ointment
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prevents neonatal eye infection from STI exposure.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: blurring is expected temporarily.

cards.title: Newborn hypoglycemia risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Risk in infants of diabetic mothers, LGA/SGA, preterm.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: jitteriness can be hypoglycemia—check glucose.

cards.title: Breastfeeding latch clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Deep latch reduces nipple trauma and improves transfer.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: pain is not ‘normal’—adjust latch.

cards.title: Breastfeeding contraindication cue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some infections/meds require guidance.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: most mothers can breastfeed—don’t discourage without reason.

cards.title: Formula mixing safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use correct water-to-formula ratio.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: over-dilution can cause hyponatremia.

cards.title: Newborn respiratory distress
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Grunting, flaring, retractions are danger signs.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘normal newborn noise’ is not retractions.

cards.title: Cyanosis check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Central cyanosis is abnormal.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: acrocyanosis (hands/feet) can be normal initially.

cards.title: Jaundice timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Early jaundice (first 24h) is concerning.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: needs evaluation; physiologic jaundice appears later.

cards.title: Kernicterus risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Very high bilirubin can cause neuro damage.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: poor feeding/lethargy with jaundice is urgent.

cards.title: Phototherapy basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Expose skin, protect eyes, monitor hydration/temp.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: turning off lights too long reduces effectiveness.

cards.title: Placenta previa sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Painless bright red bleeding.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: no vaginal exams until previa ruled out.

cards.title: Placental abruption sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Painful bleeding + rigid uterus.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: can be concealed bleed—shock signs matter.

cards.title: Shoulder dystocia action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: McRoberts maneuver and suprapubic pressure per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: fundal pressure is contraindicated.

cards.title: Amniotic fluid embolism
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sudden respiratory distress and DIC-like bleeding.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treat as emergency—support airway and circulation.

cards.title: Uterine inversion
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hemorrhage + shock after delivery with uterus displaced.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treat rapidly; don’t pull on cord aggressively.

cards.title: Group B strep newborn risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: GBS can cause neonatal sepsis.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: prophylaxis reduces risk but doesn’t eliminate—monitor newborn.

cards.title: Fundal height abnormal
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Mismatch can suggest multiple gestation or growth issue.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: needs evaluation; not a ‘normal variation’.

cards.title: Morning sickness dehydration
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Severe vomiting can cause dehydration and ketones.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: persistent vomiting needs care (hyperemesis).

cards.title: Braxton Hicks relief
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: False labor often stops with rest/hydration.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: true labor continues and changes cervix.

cards.title: Perineal care postpartum
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Front-to-back wiping reduces infection.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: tampons are avoided immediately postpartum.

cards.title: Postpartum bladder
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Full bladder prevents uterine contraction.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: assist to void if fundus is boggy/deviated.

cards.title: Afterpains
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cramping postpartum (esp multiparous/breastfeeding) is common.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: severe pain with fever suggests infection.

cards.title: Newborn cord care
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Keep stump clean/dry; it falls off naturally.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: alcohol use depends on local policy—follow guidance.

cards.title: Newborn thermoregulation sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Temp instability can signal infection.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: hypothermia can be first sign in newborns.

cards.title: ROM: infection risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prolonged ROM increases infection risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: monitor maternal temp and fetal status.

cards.title: Chorioamnionitis clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Fever, uterine tenderness, foul fluid, fetal tachycardia.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: needs antibiotics; not ‘normal labor fever’.

cards.title: Oxytocin and water intoxication
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Large amounts can cause hyponatremia.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: headache/confusion during infusion needs assessment.

cards.title: Postpartum hematoma
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Severe perineal pain/pressure with minimal bleeding.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: pain out of proportion suggests hematoma.

cards.title: Newborn weight loss
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some weight loss is normal early.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: excessive loss/dehydration signs need evaluation.

cards.title: Safe sleep
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Back to sleep, firm surface, no loose blankets.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: side sleeping is not recommended.

cards.title: Car seat teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rear-facing seat is safest for infants.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: bulky coats can prevent proper harness fit.

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: When maternal/fetal status changes, reassess vitals, bleeding, contraction pattern, and FHR.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘reassure’ without reassessment misses deterioration.

modules.title: 9. Maternal & Newborn

modules.moduleDescription: NCLEX pediatrics essentials: growth & development cues, respiratory and dehydration priorities, common infections, safety, congenital conditions basics, and pediatric med traps.

cards.title: Peds airway is priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Children desaturate faster due to smaller airways and higher O2 demand.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: mild swelling can obstruct—act early.

cards.title: Head proportion
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Infants have large heads and weak neck control.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: airway positioning matters; support head/neck.

cards.title: Fontanel assessment
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Bulging fontanel can indicate increased ICP; sunken suggests dehydration.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: crying can temporarily bulge fontanel—assess at rest.

cards.title: Stranger anxiety age
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stranger anxiety often appears around 6–12 months.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: not ‘bad behavior’—use parent presence.

cards.title: Separation anxiety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Common in toddlers.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: explain briefly; allow comfort object.

cards.title: Toddlers and autonomy
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Offer choices between two acceptable options.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: too many choices overwhelms and triggers tantrums.

cards.title: School-age coping
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: School-age respond well to concrete explanations and participation.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: talking only to parents can increase fear.

cards.title: Adolescent respect
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Provide privacy and involve them in decisions.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: discussing sensitive topics in front of parents may reduce honesty.

cards.title: Croup hallmark
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Barking cough + stridor; worse at night.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treat stridor as upper-airway emergency; calm child.

cards.title: Croup first action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Humidified air/neb epi per protocol; keep child calm.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: throat exam can worsen obstruction.

cards.title: RSV bronchiolitis hallmark
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Wheezing, tachypnea, retractions in infants.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: antibiotics don’t treat viral RSV; focus on airway/fluids.

cards.title: RSV isolation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Contact precautions are common for RSV.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: hand hygiene is key—RSV spreads easily by touch.

cards.title: Asthma in kids: silent chest
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: No wheeze with distress can be severe airflow limitation.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘quiet’ can mean impending respiratory failure.

cards.title: Peds oxygen signs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Nasal flaring, grunting, retractions indicate distress.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: cyanosis is late—don’t wait for it.

cards.title: Foreign body aspiration
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sudden cough/choking during eating/play suggests aspiration.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t do blind finger sweep—pushes object deeper.

cards.title: Epiglottitis warning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Drooling + tripod + muffled voice = emergency.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: do not inspect throat; secure airway and keep child calm.

cards.title: Dehydration early sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tachycardia and decreased tears may appear early.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: BP can stay normal until late shock.

cards.title: Best dehydration indicator
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: In infants, wet diapers/urine output is key trend.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: single diaper check misses overall pattern.

cards.title: Oral rehydration
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use ORS in small frequent amounts.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: juice/soda worsen diarrhea (high sugar).

cards.title: IV fluids priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Severe dehydration/shock needs isotonic bolus per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: hypotonic fluids are not for initial resuscitation.

cards.title: Intussusception clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Intermittent colicky pain + currant jelly stools.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: can mimic gastroenteritis—needs urgent eval.

cards.title: Pyloric stenosis clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Projectile nonbilious vomiting, hungry after, olive mass.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: metabolic alkalosis is common—check labs.

cards.title: Appendicitis in kids
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: RLQ pain, guarding; fever may develop.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: sudden pain relief can mean rupture—urgent.

cards.title: Otitis media teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Ear pain, fever; treat pain and antibiotics if ordered.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: finish antibiotics—stopping early increases relapse.

cards.title: Strep throat clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sore throat + fever + no cough suggests strep.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: untreated can lead to rheumatic fever.

cards.title: Croup vs strep sound
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Croup has barking cough/stridor; strep has sore throat.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: different airway risks—stridor is urgent.

cards.title: Kawasaki disease red flags
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Fever >5 days + rash + red eyes + strawberry tongue + swollen hands/feet.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: coronary aneurysm risk—needs urgent treatment.

cards.title: Meningitis in infants
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Irritability, poor feeding, bulging fontanel, high-pitched cry.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: lack of neck stiffness doesn’t rule out meningitis in infants.

cards.title: Varicella isolation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Airborne + contact precautions.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: immunocompromised exposure is high risk—report immediately.

cards.title: Car seat basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rear-facing as long as possible per guidelines; proper harness fit.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: bulky coat prevents secure straps.

cards.title: SIDS prevention
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Back to sleep, firm surface, no loose bedding.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: side sleeping is not recommended.

cards.title: Poisoning first action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Call Poison Control; bring container info.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: inducing vomiting is not routine and can harm.

cards.title: Lead exposure clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Old paint/dust and pica increase risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: screening is important even without symptoms.

cards.title: Drowning risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Drowning is silent and fast.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘good swimmer’ doesn’t remove need for supervision.

cards.title: Fever management
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use weight-based dosing for antipyretics.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: avoid aspirin in children (Reye risk).

cards.title: Tetralogy ‘tet spell’
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cyanotic episode relieved by knee-chest position.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: crying can trigger spells—calm and position.

cards.title: VSD sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Harsh murmur; may cause HF signs if large.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: small VSDs can close spontaneously—monitor growth.

cards.title: PDA teaching
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Patent ductus arteriosus can cause continuous ‘machine’ murmur.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: indomethacin can close PDA—monitor renal/GI effects.

cards.title: Heart failure in infants
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Poor feeding, sweating, tachypnea.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: not always ‘lazy eater’—assess for HF.

cards.title: Peds hypoglycemia sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Irritability, lethargy, sweating, seizures in severe cases.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treat promptly—brain at risk.

cards.title: Type 1 DKA clues
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss, fruity breath, Kussmaul.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: vomiting can be DKA—not just ‘stomach bug’.

cards.title: Sick day rule (kids)
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Never stop basal insulin; monitor glucose/ketones more often.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘not eating so no insulin’ can cause DKA.

cards.title: Febrile seizure basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Often brief; protect airway and safety.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: do not restrain or put anything in mouth.

cards.title: Sickle cell pain crisis
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hydration, oxygen if hypoxic, pain control.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: cold packs can vasoconstrict and worsen crisis.

cards.title: Sickle cell infection risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Functional asplenia increases infection risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: fever is emergency—seek care fast.

cards.title: Hemophilia bleeding
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Treat bleeding with factor replacement; avoid IM injections.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: aspirin/NSAIDs increase bleeding risk.

cards.title: Weight in kg only
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Peds dosing uses kg—verify weight units.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: using lb as kg is a 2.2× overdose.

cards.title: Liquid strength per 5 mL
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Many pediatric meds list mg per 5 mL.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treating as mg per 1 mL gives 5× error.

cards.title: Measuring device
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use oral syringe for accuracy.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: household spoons are inaccurate.

cards.title: Asthma triggers
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Smoke, pets, dust, exercise, infections are common triggers.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: removing triggers is as important as meds.

cards.title: Spacer use
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Spacer improves inhaler delivery in children.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: without spacer, much medication stays in mouth.

cards.title: Cystic fibrosis clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Thick secretions, recurrent lung infections, bulky stools.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: pancreatic enzymes are given with meals/snacks.

cards.title: CF airway clearance
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Chest physiotherapy and hydration help mobilize mucus.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: suppressing cough can worsen retention.

cards.title: CF salt loss
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Kids with CF can have salty sweat and dehydration risk.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: hot weather increases risk.

cards.title: Failure to thrive
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Poor weight gain can signal chronic illness or neglect.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: compare growth curves, not one weight.

cards.title: Iron deficiency anemia
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pale, fatigue; treat with iron and diet.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: iron turns stool dark—expected.

cards.title: Pinworms symptom
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Night perianal itching suggests pinworms.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treat household contacts as ordered.

cards.title: Hand-foot-mouth
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Viral rash + mouth sores; supportive care.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: antibiotics don’t help.

cards.title: Impetigo
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Honey-crusted lesions; contagious.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: teach hygiene and avoid sharing towels.

cards.title: Pertussis clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Paroxysmal cough with ‘whoop’.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: infants may have apnea rather than whoop.

cards.title: Croup cool mist
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cool mist can help mild croup.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: agitation worsens stridor—keep calm.

cards.title: Asthma peak flow zones
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Green/yellow/red guide actions.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: relying on ‘feels fine’ can miss worsening.

cards.title: Dehydration skin turgor
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Less reliable in infants—use diapers/fontanel/vitals.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘skin snaps back’ doesn’t guarantee hydration.

cards.title: Intussusception aftercare
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Air/contrast enema may reduce it; monitor recurrence.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: persistent pain after reduction needs evaluation.

cards.title: Pyloric stenosis correction
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Correct dehydration/electrolytes before surgery.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: surgery before stabilization increases risk.

cards.title: Child abuse bruising
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Bruises in non-mobile child are concerning.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: mandated reporting—don’t confront caregiver alone.

cards.title: Immunization fever
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Low-grade fever after vaccines can be expected.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: high fever or severe reaction needs evaluation.

cards.title: Live vaccine caution
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid live vaccines in severely immunocompromised kids.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: check chemo/steroid status.

cards.title: School refusal
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Can signal anxiety/depression/bullying.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: not just ‘acting out’—assess underlying cause.

cards.title: Enuresis support
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid punishment; use supportive routines.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: shame worsens anxiety and symptoms.

cards.title: Diarrhea diaper rash
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Barrier cream protects skin.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: wipes with alcohol can worsen irritation.

cards.title: RSV apnea risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Young infants can have apnea with RSV.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘no wheeze’ doesn’t mean stable—monitor breathing.

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Reassess work of breathing, hydration, and LOC when child status changes.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: children compensate then crash—don’t wait for hypotension.

modules.title: 10. Pediatrics

modules.moduleDescription: NCLEX high-yield infection control + emergencies: isolation precautions, sepsis, shock, triage, burns, wound care basics, rapid-response priorities, and common emergency traps.

cards.title: Standard precautions always
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assume all blood/body fluids potentially infectious.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: PPE is based on task/exposure risk, not diagnosis.

cards.title: Contact precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Gown + gloves for organisms spread by touch (e.g., MRSA, C. diff).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: for C. diff use soap/water—alcohol gel not enough.

cards.title: Droplet precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Mask for short-range respiratory droplets (e.g., influenza, meningitis).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: keep mask within ~3–6 feet policy; door may stay open per policy.

cards.title: Airborne precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Negative pressure + N95 for TB, measles, varicella.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: surgical mask is not enough for true airborne.

cards.title: C. diff cleaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use sporicidal disinfectant; dedicated equipment.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘looks clean’ surfaces can still spread spores.

cards.title: Hand hygiene moments
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Before/after patient contact, after removing gloves, after body fluid exposure.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: gloves do not replace hand washing.

cards.title: Sepsis early clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Suspect sepsis with infection + tachycardia, fever/hypothermia, altered LOC.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: normal BP does not rule out early shock.

cards.title: Sepsis priority actions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Obtain cultures, start broad antibiotics, give fluids per protocol quickly.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: waiting for culture results delays life-saving antibiotics.

cards.title: Lactate meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Elevated lactate suggests poor perfusion.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: lactate can rise before BP drops—act early.

cards.title: Septic shock sign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hypotension persists after fluids or needs vasopressors.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: warm skin early can still be shock.

cards.title: Vasopressor safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Give via central line when possible; monitor extravasation.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘turning up’ without correcting volume can worsen perfusion.

cards.title: Shock types overview
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hypovolemic, cardiogenic, distributive, obstructive.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treatment differs—don’t give diuretics in hypovolemic shock.

cards.title: Hypovolemic shock clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tachycardia, cool clammy skin, narrow pulse pressure.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: BP may be normal early—look at trends.

cards.title: Cardiogenic shock clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Poor pump: crackles, JVD, hypotension, cool skin.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: large fluid bolus can worsen pulmonary edema.

cards.title: Anaphylactic shock clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hives, wheeze/stridor, hypotension after exposure.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: give IM epinephrine first-line—not antihistamine.

cards.title: Neurogenic shock clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SCI with hypotension + bradycardia.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: absence of tachycardia doesn’t mean stable.

cards.title: Triage red priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Airway compromise, severe respiratory distress, shock = immediate.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: stable fractures are lower priority than breathing issues.

cards.title: Rapid Response trigger
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Acute change in LOC, RR, O2 sat, chest pain, hypotension.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘wait for next vitals’ delays escalation.

cards.title: Change in mental status
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: New confusion can signal hypoxia, sepsis, hypoglycemia, stroke.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t assume ‘dementia’—check causes.

cards.title: Hypoglycemia emergency
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Treat low glucose fast with carbs/dextrose/glucagon.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: do not give insulin for ‘high sugar’ without checking.

cards.title: Major bleeding first step
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Direct pressure and call for help.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: tourniquet is for uncontrolled severe bleeding when pressure fails.

cards.title: Internal bleeding clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tachycardia, hypotension, cool clammy skin, abdominal distention.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: normal external appearance can hide hemorrhage.

cards.title: Head injury red flags
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Worsening headache, vomiting, unequal pupils, declining LOC.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘sleeping it off’ after head injury is unsafe.

cards.title: Spinal precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Immobilize spine with trauma until cleared.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: moving patient without stabilization can worsen injury.

cards.title: Burn depth key
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Partial-thickness: blisters/pain; full-thickness: waxy/less pain.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: less pain can mean deeper burn (nerve destruction).

cards.title: Rule of nines use
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Estimate %TBSA burned for fluid resuscitation planning.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: include only partial and full thickness in TBSA calc.

cards.title: Airway burn clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Facial burns, singed nasal hair, hoarseness suggest inhalation injury.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: airway can swell later—early intubation may be needed.

cards.title: Initial burn care
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stop burning process, cool with room-temp water, cover with clean dry cloth.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ice causes vasoconstriction and tissue damage.

cards.title: Fluid resuscitation priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Large burns need aggressive fluids per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: watch urine output as perfusion indicator.

cards.title: Wound drainage types
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Serous, sanguineous, serosanguineous, purulent.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: sudden bright red drainage can signal hemorrhage.

cards.title: Dehiscence action
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cover with sterile saline-soaked gauze and call provider.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: do not push organs back in (evisceration).

cards.title: Evisceration emergency
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protect organs with moist sterile dressing, knees flexed, notify.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: patient NPO and prepare for OR.

cards.title: Pressure injury prevention
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Turn schedule, offload heels, moisture control, nutrition.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: donut cushions can worsen pressure points.

cards.title: Anaphylaxis first-line
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: IM epinephrine is first-line treatment.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: antihistamines are adjunct; don’t delay epi.

cards.title: Status asthmaticus
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Severe asthma not responding to rescue meds is emergency.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘no wheeze’ can be silent chest—impending failure.

cards.title: Pulmonary edema emergency
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sit up, O2, consider diuretics/vasodilators per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: laying flat worsens dyspnea.

cards.title: PE suspicion
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sudden SOB + pleuritic pain + tachycardia.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: normal lung sounds can still occur.

cards.title: Chest pain protocol
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess, ECG, vitals, IV access, meds per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: antacids first can delay MI care.

cards.title: Cardiac arrest response
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Start CPR and call code; defib shockable rhythms ASAP.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: checking pulse too long delays compressions.

cards.title: Vfib vs asystole
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Vfib is shockable; asystole is not.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t waste time shocking asystole.

cards.title: Poison ingestion first step
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Call Poison Control and follow instructions.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: inducing vomiting is not routine and can harm.

cards.title: Opioid overdose priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Support airway/ventilation; naloxone as ordered.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: oxygen is still needed after naloxone.

cards.title: CO poisoning clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Headache, cherry-red (rare), exposure history.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: pulse ox can read normal—give 100% O2.

cards.title: Hyperkalemia ECG clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Peaked T waves, widened QRS.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treat urgently—don’t wait for repeat labs.

cards.title: Hypokalemia risk
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: U waves, dysrhythmias, muscle weakness.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: IV K+ is never IV push.

cards.title: Hyponatremia seizures
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Severe low Na+ can cause seizures.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: correct slowly to avoid osmotic demyelination.

cards.title: Fever in neutropenia
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Fever in chemo patient is emergency.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: avoid rectal temps/suppositories (bleeding/infection risk).

cards.title: Sepsis bundles timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Many protocols target antibiotics within 1 hour.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: delays worsen mortality risk.

cards.title: Falls after anticoagulants
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Head injury on anticoagulants needs urgent evaluation.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘no symptoms’ doesn’t rule out bleed.

cards.title: Stroke mimic check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Check glucose—hypoglycemia can mimic stroke.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: treat glucose first if low.

cards.title: Tension pneumothorax clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Severe distress + tracheal deviation + hypotension.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: needle decompression may be needed before imaging per protocol.

cards.title: Chest tube clamp trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Do not clamp a chest tube routinely.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: clamping can cause tension pneumothorax unless ordered for troubleshooting.

cards.title: SVT management idea
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If unstable, synchronized cardioversion per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: vagal maneuvers only for stable patient.

cards.title: Heat stroke
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hot, dry skin + AMS requires rapid cooling.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: antipyretics don’t fix heat stroke.

cards.title: Hypothermia rewarming
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Rewarm gradually; handle gently.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: rough handling can trigger dysrhythmias.

cards.title: DKA vs HHS neuro
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: HHS often has more neuro changes due to hyperosmolarity.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: both need fluids; don’t delay.

cards.title: Seizure active care
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protect head, turn side, time, do not restrain.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t put anything in mouth.

cards.title: Post-op hemorrhage clue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Restlessness and tachycardia can be early signs.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: hypotension is late—inspect dressings/drains.

cards.title: Compartment syndrome
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pain out of proportion, paresthesia, pallor, pulselessness late.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t elevate high; keep at heart level and notify.

cards.title: Crush injury hyperK
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Crush injuries can cause hyperkalemia from cell lysis.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: monitor ECG and labs early.

cards.title: Drowning: aspiration
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Monitor for delayed respiratory distress after near-drowning.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘seems fine’ can deteriorate later.

cards.title: Severe allergic reaction with ACE
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Angioedema can obstruct airway.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: swelling tongue/lips needs emergency airway readiness.

cards.title: Blood transfusion reaction
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stop transfusion, keep line open NS, assess, notify.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: do not flush blood into patient.

cards.title: TRALI vs TACO hint
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: TRALI often with fever/hypotension; TACO with HTN/JVD.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: both cause SOB—monitor closely.

cards.title: Bleeding precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid IM injections and minimize sticks when bleeding risk high.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘one more lab’ can worsen bleeding.

cards.title: Isolation PPE order
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Don PPE before entry; remove before exit; hand hygiene after.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: touching face with contaminated gloves spreads pathogens.

cards.title: Sharps safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Never recap needles; use safety devices.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: recapping is common cause of needle sticks.

cards.title: Needle stick first step
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Wash area, report immediately, follow protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: squeezing wound aggressively isn’t recommended.

cards.title: Antibiotics culture timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cultures first when possible, then antibiotics fast.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t delay antibiotics if unstable.

cards.title: Sepsis: urine output
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Urine output <0.5 mL/kg/hr suggests poor perfusion.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: one void doesn’t prove adequate perfusion.

cards.title: Emergency reassess #71
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: In any emergency, reassess ABCs, vitals, and response after each intervention.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: doing interventions without reassessment misses failure.

modules.title: 11. Infection Control & Emergency

modules.moduleDescription: NCLEX leadership essentials: delegation (RN vs PN/LVN vs UAP), prioritization, assignment, safety/quality, incident reporting, communication, and legal/ethical traps.

cards.title: ABCs vs Maslow
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ABCs and safety come first, then higher-level needs.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: pain control is important, but airway/bleeding outrank it.

cards.title: Unstable vs stable
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Unstable/acute changes are priority over stable chronic problems.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘new confusion’ beats routine med pass.

cards.title: Actual vs potential
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Actual problems (bleeding, hypoxia) generally outrank potential ones.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: potential risk still wins if catastrophic and imminent.

cards.title: Time-sensitive meds
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Time-critical meds (insulin, antibiotics, anticoags) must be on time.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: delaying antibiotics in sepsis is high-risk.

cards.title: Least invasive first
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Start with least invasive effective intervention when appropriate.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t choose ‘teach’ when patient is unstable.

cards.title: Post-op day 0 priorities
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Airway, breathing, circulation, pain, bleeding, urine output.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ambulation teaching is not first if hypotensive.

cards.title: Delegate vs assign
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Delegation transfers task; RN retains accountability.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: you can’t delegate responsibility—only tasks.

cards.title: RN tasks
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: RN must do assessment, teaching, evaluation, and unstable care.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: UAP cannot interpret data or triage.

cards.title: UAP tasks
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: UAP can do routine, predictable tasks (VS, ADLs, ambulation).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: do not delegate assessment or first-time tasks.

cards.title: PN/LVN scope general
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: PN can do stable patient care and some meds per policy; RN evaluates.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: PN typically should not manage unstable/complex assessments.

cards.title: Five Rights of Delegation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Right task, circumstance, person, direction, supervision.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: missing ‘supervision’ is a classic NCLEX wrong answer.

cards.title: Clear directions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Give specific instructions: what, when, what to report.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘let me know if anything changes’ is too vague.

cards.title: Follow-up required
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: RN must evaluate outcomes after delegation.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: assuming task done correctly is unsafe.

cards.title: Initial assessment rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Initial assessment is RN-only.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: UAP can collect VS but RN interprets and assesses meaning.

cards.title: Unstable patient care
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Unstable/acute change patients require RN attention.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: delegating dyspnea assessment is unsafe.

cards.title: Teaching rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Patient education is RN responsibility (and some PN per policy).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: UAP can reinforce, not teach new content.

cards.title: Evaluation rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Evaluating response to meds/interventions is RN task.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: UAP reporting ‘patient feels better’ is not evaluation.

cards.title: Best assignment: new grad
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Give predictable, stable patients to new nurse.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: avoid complex drips, fresh post-op, unstable neuro.

cards.title: Best assignment: float nurse
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Float nurse gets patients with common diagnoses and clear routines.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: avoid giving float the unit’s most complex specialty case.

cards.title: Best assignment: PN/LVN
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assign stable patients requiring routine meds and care.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: avoid new admissions needing full assessment.

cards.title: Best assignment: UAP
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assign ADLs, transport, I&O, routine VS.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: do not assign sterile procedures or care plans.

cards.title: UAP can obtain VS
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: UAP may take VS on stable patients.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: RN must assess abnormal VS and decide actions.

cards.title: UAP and glucose checks
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: UAP can perform fingerstick per policy.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: RN/licensed nurse must interpret and treat abnormal results.

cards.title: UAP and postop ambulation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: UAP can ambulate stable patient with clear instructions.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: first ambulation after surgery may require RN assessment.

cards.title: PN giving meds
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: PN can administer routine meds to stable patients per policy.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: titrated IV drips often RN-only.

cards.title: PN and wound care
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: PN can perform dressing changes for stable wounds.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: complex wound VAC/first-time teaching is RN.

cards.title: Who to see first?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: See the patient with ABC compromise or acute change first.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: lab value questions—assess the patient if symptomatic.

cards.title: New chest pain on unit
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Treat as priority—assess, ECG, vitals, protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t delegate chest-pain assessment.

cards.title: Post-op bleeding
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Large fresh drainage + tachycardia = priority.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘reinforce dressing’ may hide bleeding—assess and notify.

cards.title: Confusion in elderly
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Acute confusion can be hypoxia, infection, hypoglycemia.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t label as ‘sundowning’ without assessment.

cards.title: High K+ priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Verify, assess ECG, act per protocol.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: giving potassium supplements is dangerous.

cards.title: SBAR structure
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: calling provider without recommendation wastes time.

cards.title: Read-back orders
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Repeat back verbal/telephone orders.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘I think I heard…’ is not safe—clarify.

cards.title: Critical labs reporting
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Report critical values promptly per policy.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: waiting for routine rounds delays intervention.

cards.title: Handoff essentials
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Include diagnosis, recent changes, pending tests, risks, priorities.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: omitting ‘code status’ is a safety error.

cards.title: Incident report purpose
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Documents unusual events for quality improvement.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: not part of medical record; don’t chart ‘incident report filed’ (policy-dependent).

cards.title: Charting facts only
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Document objective data and actions taken.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: avoid blame words like ‘careless’ or ‘lazy’.

cards.title: Informed consent role
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Provider explains procedure; nurse witnesses signature and verifies understanding.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: nurse doesn’t ‘get consent’ by explaining risks/benefits.

cards.title: Refusal of care
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Competent adult can refuse treatment.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: educate on risks, notify provider, document; don’t coerce.

cards.title: Confidentiality
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Share info only with care team; follow HIPAA.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: discussing patients in elevators is a violation.

cards.title: Mandatory reporting
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Report suspected abuse/neglect per law/policy.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: you don’t need proof to report suspicion.

cards.title: Advance directives
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Honor advance directives and verify code status.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: family can’t override competent patient’s wishes.

cards.title: Independent double-check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: High-alert meds need independent verification (insulin, heparin).
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘I already checked’ isn’t independent.

cards.title: Look-alike sound-alike meds
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use barcode, verify name/dose/route.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: relying on vial color causes errors.

cards.title: Medication error response
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess patient, notify provider, follow policy, document objectively.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: hiding error is unethical and unsafe.

cards.title: Root cause analysis
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: RCA finds system causes after sentinel events.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: it’s not for blaming individuals.

cards.title: Sentinel event meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Unexpected death/serious harm triggers investigation.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: near-miss still needs reporting but may not be sentinel.

cards.title: Patient identification
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use 2 identifiers before meds/blood/procedures.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: room number is not an identifier.

cards.title: Fall risk precautions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Call light, bed low, nonskid, frequent rounding.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘patient said they’re fine’ doesn’t remove fall risk.

cards.title: Restraint documentation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Need order/time limits/monitoring and least restrictive first.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: restraints for convenience are illegal/unethical.

cards.title: Time-out procedure
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Verify patient/procedure/site before invasive procedures.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: marking site alone is not a time-out.

cards.title: Transfusion safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Verify blood with 2 staff; monitor for reaction early.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: leaving patient alone at start of transfusion is unsafe.

cards.title: Chain of command
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Escalate safety concerns up the chain when needed.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: stopping after one refusal can risk patient safety.

cards.title: Unprofessional behavior
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Address safety impact and use proper reporting channels.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: arguing in front of patient undermines trust.

cards.title: Delegation conflict
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If delegate refuses, clarify task and safety rationale; reassign if needed.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ignoring refusal leaves care undone.

cards.title: Who first: post-op with stridor vs stable pain?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Airway compromise is first.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: pain management is important but cannot precede airway.

cards.title: Who first: diabetic shaky vs chronic HTN?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Suspect hypoglycemia—treat now.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: chronic issues are lower priority than acute neuro signs.

cards.title: Who first: new SOB after surgery vs routine dressing change?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: New SOB suggests PE/atelectasis—assess now.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: routine tasks can wait.

cards.title: Who first: high fever on chemo vs mild nausea?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Neutropenic fever is emergency.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: nausea is uncomfortable but not as time-critical.

cards.title: Who first: chest tube continuous bubbling vs stable O2?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Continuous bubbling suggests air leak—assess system promptly.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t clamp tube; check connections.

cards.title: Best to delegate: stable patient bath
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: UAP can assist with hygiene for stable patients.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: avoid giving UAP unstable or new-onset symptoms.

cards.title: Delegate: newly admitted CHF assessment?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: RN must do admission assessment.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: UAP can get weight/VS but RN assesses.

cards.title: Delegate: routine VS on stable patient
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: UAP appropriate with clear report parameters.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: RN must respond to abnormal findings.

cards.title: Delegate: teaching insulin injection
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: RN teaches new skill.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: UAP can reinforce after teaching, not teach initial.

cards.title: Assign to PN: stable UTI antibiotics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: PN can care for stable patient with routine meds.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: avoid titrated drips/unstable respiratory.

cards.title: Assign to new grad: stable postop day 2
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Predictable care is best for new grad.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: fresh trach or unstable neuro is too complex.

cards.title: First after med error discovered
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Assess patient and vitals first.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: calling manager before patient assessment is wrong order.

cards.title: Charting after fall
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Document objectively: what happened, assessment, interventions.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t blame patient or staff in chart.

cards.title: Family asks for info
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Verify permission/POA; protect confidentiality.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘they’re family’ doesn’t guarantee access.

cards.title: Unsafe order concern
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use chain of command if provider won’t clarify.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: carrying out unsafe order makes you liable.

cards.title: Incident report content
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Include facts and actions, not opinions.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: don’t put incident report in medical record.

cards.title: Critical lab call
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Repeat/read-back and document per policy.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: delaying callback risks patient harm.

cards.title: Handoff priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Communicate changes, risks, and pending tests.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: leaving out allergies/code status is unsafe.

cards.title: Restraint removal
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Remove ASAP when safe and criteria met.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: leaving restraints ‘just in case’ violates least restriction.

cards.title: Patient refuses blood
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Respect refusal, educate, notify, document.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: coercion violates autonomy.

cards.title: Documentation timing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Chart as soon as possible after care.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: charting late increases errors and legal risk.

cards.title: Late entry rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If late entry, label as late with date/time per policy.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: never alter prior documentation.

cards.title: Electronic chart copy-forward
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Verify copied data is still accurate.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: copy-forward errors are common legal issues.

cards.title: Delegation: abnormal blood sugar
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: RN should assess and treat abnormal glucose.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: UAP reports result; RN decides intervention.

cards.title: Delegation: I&O for stable patient
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: UAP can measure and record I&O.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: RN interprets trends and addresses low urine output.

cards.title: Assignment: isolation patient
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Give to nurse with appropriate training and workload.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: assigning multiple contact isolation rooms to one nurse may increase contamination risk.

cards.title: Safety rounds
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Frequent rounding reduces falls and improves satisfaction.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: relying only on bed alarm is insufficient.

cards.title: Priority: airway after sedation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Monitor airway and RR closely after sedatives/opioids.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: pulse ox alone may miss hypoventilation.

cards.title: Telephone order safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Read-back and clarify dose/route/time.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘sounds right’ is not verification.

cards.title: Cultural humility
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Ask patient preferences and avoid assumptions.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: stereotyping harms trust and care quality.

cards.title: Ethics consult
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use ethics resources for conflicts about goals of care.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: delaying when conflict escalates harms team/patient.

cards.title: HIPAA social media
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Never post patient info/photos.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: ‘no name’ still can identify patient.

cards.title: Medication reconciliation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Verify home meds on admission and discharge.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: missing med rec causes many adverse events.

cards.title: Discharge planning early
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Start planning on admission for complex patients.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: last-minute planning increases readmissions.

cards.title: Leadership check #90
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Reassess priorities after each new symptom, order, or result.
Takeaway/Trap: Trap: sticking to original plan can miss rapid deterioration.
